      <td style="width: auto; font-size: 9pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">0.6%</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">0.0%</em>&#160;the Company's total assets on a cost and fair value basis, respectively,&#160;are in&#160;non-qualifying assets under Section <em style="font: inherit;">55</em>(a) of the <em style="font: inherit;">1940</em> Act. Under the <em style="font: inherit;">1940</em> Act, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> acquire any non-qualifying assets unless, at the time the acquisition is made, qualifying assets represent at least <em style="font: inherit;">70%</em> of the Company&#8217;s total assets.</p> </td>

Interest will accrue during the life of the debt investment on each ETP and will be recognized as non-cash income until it is actually paid. Therefore, a portion of the incentive fee the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>pay its Advisor will be based on income that the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet received in cash.</p> </td>

      <td style="width: auto; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify;">The investment originally consisted of debt investments in Evelo Biosciences Inc. (&#8220;Evelo&#8221;). Evelo was a clinical stage life science company that was unable to raise additional capital to continue as a going concern and, through a series of transactions, Evelo became a subsidiary of Evelo Holdings, Inc. (&#8220;Evelo Holdings&#8221;) and Evelo Holdings assumed the indebtedness of Evelo to the Company.&#160; Evelo Holdings is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> an operating company but holds certain contractual rights to contingent payments and owns equity in Evelo, as well as certain assets it seeks to sell. The Company has a <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> priority security interest in the assets of Evelo Holdings, so if any payments are received by Evelo Holdings or any of its equity holdings or other assets are sold, the Company will receive substantially all of the proceeds from the same, until such time, if ever, that all of the indebtedness is repaid. Accordingly, the Company characterizes this investment as an &#8220;Other Investment&#8221; rather than a &#8220;Debt Investment".</td>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:OrganizationConsolidationAndPresentationOfFinancialStatementsDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3175311" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="notes" title="notes" href="#"></a>Note</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> Organization</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Horizon Technology Finance Corporation (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) was organized as a Delaware corporation on <em style="font: inherit;"> March&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">16,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2010</em> and is an externally managed, non-diversified, closed-end investment company. The Company has elected to be regulated as a business development company (&#8220;BDC&#8221;) under the <em style="font: inherit;">1940</em> Act. In addition, for tax purposes, the Company has elected to be treated as a regulated investment company (&#8220;RIC&#8221;) as defined under Subchapter M of the Internal Revenue Code of <em style="font: inherit;">1986,</em> as amended (the &#8220;Code&#8221;). As a RIC, the Company generally is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to corporate-level federal income tax on the portion of its taxable income (including net capital gains) the Company distributes to its stockholders. The Company primarily makes secured debt investments to development-stage companies in the technology, life science, healthcare information and services and sustainability industries. All of the Company&#8217;s debt investments consist of loans secured by all of, or a portion of, the applicable debtor company&#8217;s tangible and intangible assets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> October&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">28,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2010,</em> the Company completed an initial public offering (&#8220;IPO&#8221;) and its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol &#8220;HRZN&#8221;.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> April 14, 2026, </em>the Company completed its previously announced merger with Monroe Capital Corporation (&#8220;MRCC&#8221;), HMMS, Inc. (&#8220;Merger Sub&#8221;), Monroe Capital BDC Advisors, LLC, and the Advisor, pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated as of <em style="font: inherit;"> August 7, 2025 (</em>the &#8220;Merger Agreement&#8221;). Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, immediately following the Asset Sale (as defined below) and at the effective time of the Merger (the &#8220;Effective Time&#8221;), Merger Sub merged with and into MRCC, with MRCC continuing as the surviving company and as a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, and, immediately thereafter, MRCC merged &#160;into the Company, with the Company&#160;continuing as the surviving company (collectively, the &#8220;Mergers&#8221;).&#160;MRCC also entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement (the &#8220;Asset Purchase Agreement&#8221;) with Monroe Capital Income Plus Corporation (&#8220;MCIP&#8221;), and MC Advisors, pursuant to which, MCIP acquired all of MRCC&#8217;s investment assets and liabilities at fair value, for cash (the &#8220;Asset Sale&#8221; and together with the Merger, the &#8220;Transactions&#8221;).</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Horizon Credit II LLC (&#8220;Credit II&#8221;) was formed as a Delaware limited liability company on <em style="font: inherit;"> June&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">28,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2011,</em> with the Company as its sole equity member. Credit II is a special purpose bankruptcy-remote entity and is a separate legal entity from the Company. Any assets conveyed to Credit II are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available to creditors of the Company or any other entity other than Credit II&#8217;s lenders. Credit II is consolidated in the financial statements of the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Horizon Funding I, LLC (&#8220;HFI&#8221;) was formed as a Delaware limited liability company on <em style="font: inherit;"> May 9, 2018, </em>with Horizon Secured Loan Fund I LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (&#8220;HSLFI&#8221;) as its sole member. HFI is a special purpose bankruptcy-remote entity and is a separate legal entity from HSLFI. Any assets conveyed to HFI are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available to creditors of HSLFI or any other entity other than HFI&#8217;s lenders. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> April 21, 2020, </em>HSLFI and its subsidiary, HFI, are consolidated in the financial statements of the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">Horizon Funding II, LLC (&#8220;HFII&#8221;) was formed as a Delaware limited liability company o</span>n&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 13, </em><em style="font: inherit;">20</em><span style="background-color:#ffffff;"><em style="font: inherit;">24,</em> with the Company as its sole equity member. H</span>FII is a special purpose bankruptcy-remote entity and is a separate legal entity from the Company. Any assets conveyed to HFII are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available to creditors of the Company or any other entity other than HFII&#8217;s lenders.&#160;HFII&#160;is consolidated in the financial statements of the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company has established wholly owned subsidiaries, which are&#160;structured as&#160;Delaware limited liability companies, either to hold assets of portfolio companies&#160;acquired in connection with a foreclosure or bankruptcy or to hold equity in portfolio companies which the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>control. Such wholly-owned subsidiaries are separate legal entities&#160;from the Company and are consolidated in the financial statements of the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company, together with a former co-lender to IMV, established HIMV LLC, a Delaware limited liability company to purchase and sell the assets of IMV, a past borrower of the Company. The assets of IMV were sold for (i) the right to receive certain payments, if any, in connection with the potential future development and licensing of the assets sold and (ii) equity in the buyer of such assets. HIMV LLC was&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144286650" contextRef="i_2025-08-05_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-HorizonTechnologyFinanceCorporationMember_OwnershipAxis-HIMVLLCMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByParent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">70</ix:nonFraction>% owned by the Company and <ix:nonFraction id="c144286651" contextRef="i_2025-08-05_LegalEntityAxis-ColenderMember_OwnershipAxis-HIMVLLCMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByNoncontrollingOwners" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">30</ix:nonFraction>% owned by a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party&#160;co-lender. On <em style="font: inherit;"> August 6, 2025, </em>the Company purchased&#160;its co-lender&#8217;s interest in HIMV LLC.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> August 6, 2025, </em>the Company owns <ix:nonFraction id="c144286653" contextRef="i_2025-08-06_OwnershipAxis-HIMVLLCMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByParent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of HIMV LLC and HIMV LLC is consolidated in the financial statements of the Company. The Company dissolved HIMV LLC on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 27, 2026.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company&#8217;s investment strategy is to maximize the investment portfolio&#8217;s return by generating current income from the debt investments the Company makes and capital appreciation from the warrants the Company receives when making such debt investments. The Company has entered into an investment management agreement (the&#160;&#8220;Investment Management Agreement&#8221;) with the Advisor&#160;under which the Advisor manages the day-to-day operations of, and provides investment advisory services to, the Company.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:BasisOfPresentationAndSignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" id="c3175312" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">2.</em> Basis of presentation and significant accounting policies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The consolidated financial statements of the Company have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) and pursuant to the requirements for reporting on Form&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10&#8209;Q</em> and Articles <em style="font: inherit;">6</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> of Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X</em> (&#8220;Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X&#8221;</em>) under the Securities Act of <em style="font: inherit;">1933,</em> as amended (the &#8220;Securities Act&#8221;). In the opinion of management, the consolidated financial statements reflect all adjustments and reclassifications, consisting solely of normal recurring accruals, that are necessary for the fair presentation of financial results as of and for the periods presented. All intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated. The current period&#8217;s results of operations are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of results that ultimately <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be achieved for the&#160;year. Therefore, the unaudited financial statements and notes should be read in conjunction with the audited financial statements and notes thereto as of and for the&#160;year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="c144306648" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Principles of consolidation</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">As required under GAAP and Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X,</em> the Company will generally consolidate its investment in a company that is an investment company subsidiary or a controlled operating company whose business consists of providing services to the Company. Accordingly, the Company consolidated the results of the Company&#8217;s wholly-owned subsidiaries in its consolidated financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Assets related to transactions that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) Topic <em style="font: inherit;">860,</em> <i>Transfers and Servicing </i>requirements for accounting sale treatment are reflected in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Assets and Liabilities as investments. Those assets are owned by special purpose entities&#160;that are consolidated in the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements. The creditors of the special purpose entities have received security interests in such assets, and such assets are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> intended to be available to the creditors of the Company (or any affiliate of the Company).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c144306650" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Use of estimates</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In preparing the consolidated financial statements in accordance with GAAP, management is required to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, and disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities, as of the date of the balance sheet and income and expenses for the period. Actual results could differ from those estimates. Material estimates that are particularly susceptible to significant change in the near term relate to the valuation of investments.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c144306651" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Fair value</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company records all of its investments at fair value in accordance with relevant GAAP, which establishes a framework used to measure fair value and requires disclosures for fair value measurements. The Company has categorized its investments carried at fair value, based on the priority of the valuation technique, into a <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-level fair value hierarchy as more fully described in Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">6.</em> Fair value is a market-based measure considered from the perspective of the market participant who holds the financial instrument rather than an entity specific measure. Therefore, when market assumptions are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> readily available, the Company&#8217;s own assumptions are set to reflect those that management believes market participants would use in pricing the financial instrument at the measurement date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The availability of observable inputs can vary depending on the financial instrument and is affected by a wide variety of factors, including, for example, the type of product, whether the product is new, whether the product is traded on an active exchange or in the secondary market and the current market conditions. To the extent that the valuation is based on models or inputs that are less observable or unobservable in the market, the determination of fair value requires more judgment. Accordingly, the degree of judgment exercised by the Company in determining fair value is greatest for financial instruments classified as Level <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">See Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">6</em> for additional information regarding fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c144306652" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Segments</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company has determined that it has a single reporting segment and operating unit structure. The Company lends to and invests in portfolio companies in various technology, life science, healthcare information and services and sustainability industries. The Company separately evaluates the performance of each of its lending and investment relationships. However, because each of these debt investments and investment relationships has similar business and economic characteristics, they have been aggregated into a single lending and investment segment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The chief operating decision maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;)&#160;is comprised of the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Investment Officer. The CODM assesses the performance of and makes operating decisions on behalf of the Company on a consolidated basis primarily based on the Company&#8217;s net increase (decrease) in net assets resulting from operations (&#8220;net income&#8221;). In addition to numerous other factors and metrics, the CODM utilizes net income as a key metric in recommending to the Company's board of directors (the &#8220;Board&#8221;) the amount of dividends to be distributed to the Company&#8217;s stockholders and the Board makes the determination of the amount of dividends to be distributed to the Company&#8217;s stockholders. As the Company&#8217;s operations comprise a single reporting segment, the segment assets are reflected on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Assets and Liabilities as &#8220;Total assets&#8221; and the significant segment expenses are listed on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:InvestmentPolicyTextBlock" id="c144306653" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Investments</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Investments are recorded at fair value. Pursuant to the amended SEC Rule <em style="font: inherit;">2a</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">5</em> of the <em style="font: inherit;">1940</em> Act, on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 29, 2022, </em>the Board&#160;designated the Advisor as the Company&#8217;s &#8220;valuation designee.&#8221; The valuation designee determines the fair value of the Company&#8217;s portfolio investments and the Company's Board&#160;oversees the valuation designee. The Company has the intent to hold its debt investments for the foreseeable future or until maturity or payoff.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Interest on debt investments is accrued and included in income based on contractual rates applied to principal amounts outstanding. Interest income is determined using a method that results in a level rate of return on principal amounts outstanding. Generally, when a debt investment becomes <em style="font: inherit;">90</em>&#160;days or more past due, or if the Company otherwise does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect to receive interest and principal repayments, the debt investment is placed on non-accrual status and the recognition of interest income <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be discontinued. Interest payments received on non-accrual debt investments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be recognized as income, on a cash basis, or applied to principal depending upon management&#8217;s judgment at the time the debt investment is placed on non-accrual status. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, there were&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> investments on nonaccrual status with a cost of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286703" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-ThreeInvestmentsMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:InvestmentsCostNonaccrualStatus" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">32.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and a fair value of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286704" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-ThreeInvestmentsMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:InvestmentsFairValueNonaccrualStatus" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">24.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, there were <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> investments on non-accrual status with a cost of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286706" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-FourInvestmentsMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:InvestmentsCostNonaccrualStatus" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">32.8</ix:nonFraction> million and a fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286707" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-FourInvestmentsMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:InvestmentsFairValueNonaccrualStatus" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">24.5</ix:nonFraction> million. For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the Company recognized&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286709" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:InvestmentsNonaccrualInterestIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of interest income from&#160;debt investments while on non-accrual status.&#160;For the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em>, the Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286711">not</span> recognize any interest income from debt investments while on non-accrual status.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">From time to time, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have debt investments&#160;that contain a PIK provision. Contractual PIK interest, which represents contractually deferred interest added to the loan balance that is generally due at the end of the loan term, is generally recorded on an accrual basis to the extent such amounts are expected to be collected. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, there were&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em>&#160;investments with PIK provisions.&#160;For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, PIK interest income totaled&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286715" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeOperatingPaidInKind" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.3</ix:nonFraction> million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286716" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeOperatingPaidInKind" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.&#160;For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>,&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144286719" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:InvestmentIncomeAttributableToNoncashPaidinkindInterestPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">5.3</ix:nonFraction>% and<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144286720" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:InvestmentIncomeAttributableToNoncashPaidinkindInterestPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">1.2</ix:nonFraction>%,</span> respectively, of the Company&#8217;s total investment income was attributable to non-cash PIK interest. The Company will generally cease accruing PIK interest if management does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect the portfolio company to be able to pay all principal and interest due. For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, there were <ix:nonFraction id="c144286723" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-ZeroInvestmentsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeOperatingPaidInKind" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction>&#160;debt investments which had accrued PIK interest into income during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;placed on nonaccrual status as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>.&#160;For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;debt investment, which had accrued PIK interest into income of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286727" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31_InvestmentTypeAxis-OneInvestmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeOperatingPaidInKind" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em> was placed on nonaccrual status as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company receives a variety of fees from borrowers in the ordinary course of conducting its business, including advisory fees, commitment fees, amendment fees, non-utilization fees, success fees and prepayment fees. In a limited number of cases, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also receive a non-refundable deposit earned upon the termination of a transaction. Debt investment origination fees, net of certain direct origination costs, are deferred and, along with unearned income, are amortized as a level-yield adjustment over the respective term of the debt investment. All other income is recognized when earned. Fees for counterparty debt investment commitments with multiple debt investments are allocated to each debt investment based upon each debt investment&#8217;s relative fair value. When a debt investment is placed on non-accrual status, the amortization of the related fees and unearned income is discontinued until the debt investment is returned to accrual status.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Certain debt investment agreements also require the borrower to make an ETP, that is accrued into interest receivable and taken into income over the life of the debt investment to the extent such amounts are expected to be collected. The Company will generally cease accruing the income if there is insufficient value to support the accrual or the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect the borrower to be able to pay the ETP when due. The proportion of the Company&#8217;s total investment income that resulted from the portion of ETPs <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> received in cash for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> was&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144286733" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:InvestmentNonaccrualIncomeNotReceivedInCashPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">6.0</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction id="c144286734" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:InvestmentNonaccrualIncomeNotReceivedInCashPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">4.6</ix:nonFraction>%, respectively.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In connection with substantially all lending arrangements, the Company receives warrants to purchase shares of stock from the borrower. The warrants are recorded as assets at estimated fair value on the grant date using the Black-Scholes valuation model. The warrants are considered loan fees and are recorded as unearned income on the grant date. The unearned income is recognized as interest income over the contractual life of the related debt investment in accordance with the Company&#8217;s income recognition policy. Subsequent to debt investment origination, the fair value of the warrants is determined using the Black-Scholes valuation model. Any adjustment to fair value is recorded through earnings as net unrealized appreciation or depreciation on investments. Gains and losses from the disposition of the warrants or stock acquired from the exercise of warrants are recognized as realized gains and losses on investments.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Realized gains or losses on the sale of investments, or upon the determination that an investment balance, or portion thereof, is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recoverable, are calculated using the specific identification method. The Company measures realized gains or losses by calculating the difference between the net proceeds from the repayment or sale and the amortized cost basis of the investment. Net unrealized appreciation or depreciation reflects the change in the fair values of the Company&#8217;s portfolio investments during the reporting period, including any reversal of previously recorded unrealized appreciation or depreciation when gains or losses are realized.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:DebtPolicyTextBlock" id="c144306654" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Debt issuance costs</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Debt issuance costs are fees and other direct incremental costs incurred by the Company in obtaining debt financing from its lenders and issuing debt securities. The unamortized balance of debt issuance costs as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286737" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8.8</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286738" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">10.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively. These amounts are capitalized and amortized and included in interest expense in the consolidated statements of operations over the life of the borrowings. The accumulated amortization balances as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> were&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286739" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccumulatedAmortizationDeferredFinanceCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.6</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286740" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccumulatedAmortizationDeferredFinanceCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively. The amortization expense for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;was $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286743" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfFinancingCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286744" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfFinancingCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c144306655" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Income taxes</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">As a BDC, the Company has elected to be treated as a RIC under Subchapter M of the Code and operates in a manner so as to qualify for the tax treatment applicable to RICs. In order to qualify as a RIC and to avoid the imposition of corporate-level income tax on the portion of its taxable income distributed to stockholders, among other things, the Company is required to meet certain source of income and asset diversification requirements and to timely distribute dividends out of assets legally available for distribution to its stockholders of an amount generally at least equal to <em style="font: inherit;">90%</em> of its investment company taxable income, as defined by the Code and determined without regard to any deduction for dividends paid, for each tax&#160;year. The Company, among other things, has made and intends to continue to make the requisite distributions to its stockholders, which generally relieves the Company from corporate-level U.S. federal income taxes. Accordingly, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> provision for federal income tax has been recorded in the financial statements. Differences between taxable income and net increase in net assets resulting from operations either can be temporary, meaning they will reverse in the future, or permanent. In accordance with ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">946,</em> <i>Financial Services</i>&#8212;<i>Investment Companies</i>, as amended, of the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;), permanent tax differences, such as non-deductible excise taxes paid, are reclassified from distributions in excess of net investment income and net realized loss on investments to paid-in-capital at the end of each fiscal&#160;year. These permanent book-to-tax differences are reclassified on the consolidated statements of changes in net assets to reflect their tax character but have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> impact on total net assets.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Depending on the level of taxable income earned in a tax&#160;year, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>choose to carry forward taxable income in excess of current&#160;year distributions into the next tax&#160;year and incur a <ix:nonFraction id="c144286749" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:FederalExciseTaxPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4</ix:nonFraction>% U.S. federal excise tax on such income, as required. To the extent that the Company determines that its estimated current&#160;year annual taxable income will be in excess of estimated current&#160;year distributions, the Company accrues excise tax, if any, on estimated excess taxable income as taxable income is earned. For the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>,&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286752" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ExciseAndSalesTaxes" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286753" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ExciseAndSalesTaxes" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, was accrued for U.S. federal excise tax.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company evaluates tax positions taken in the course of preparing the Company&#8217;s tax returns to determine whether the tax positions are &#8220;more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not&#8221;</em> to be sustained by the applicable tax authority in accordance with ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740,</em> <i>Income Taxes</i>, as modified by ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">946.</em> Tax benefits of positions <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> deemed to meet the more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> threshold, or uncertain tax positions, would be recorded as a tax expense in the current&#160;year. It is the Company&#8217;s policy to recognize accrued interest and penalties related to uncertain tax benefits in income tax expense. The Company had <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286760"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286761">no</span></span> material uncertain tax positions at <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. The Company&#8217;s income tax returns for the <em style="font: inherit;">2026,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286764">2024</span> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;tax&#160;years remain subject to examination by U.S. federal and state tax authorities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="hrzn:DistributionsPolicyTextBlock" id="c144306656" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Distributions</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2026, </em>the Company recorded distributions to common stockholders on the date the distribution was declared by the&#160;Board. On and after <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2026, </em>the Company records distributions to common stockholders on the ex-dividend date for such distribution. The Board continually monitors and reassesses the amount of cash&#160;to be paid out as distributions relative to the net investment income generated by the Company and other metrics.&#160;Net realized capital gains, if any, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be distributed, although the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>decide to retain such net realized gains for investment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company has adopted a dividend reinvestment plan that provides for reinvestment of cash distributions on behalf of its stockholders, unless a stockholder elects to receive cash. As a result, if the Board declares a cash distribution, then stockholders who have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> &#8220;opted out&#8221; of the dividend reinvestment plan will have their cash distributions automatically reinvested in additional shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock, rather than receiving the cash distribution. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue new shares or purchase shares in the open market to fulfill its obligations under the plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityPolicyTextBlock" id="c144306657" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Stockholders</i></b>&#8217;<b><i> Equity</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 22, 2023, </em>the Company&#160;entered into an At-The-Market (&#8220;ATM&#8221;) sales agreement&#160;(the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2023</em>&#160;Equity Distribution Agreement&#8221;), with Goldman Sachs&#160;&amp; Co. LLC and B. Riley FBR,&#160;Inc.&#160;(each a &#8220;Sales Agent&#8221; and, collectively, the &#8220;Sales Agents&#8221;). The <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> Equity Distribution Agreement provides that the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>offer and sell its shares of its common stock from time to time through the Sales Agents up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286769" contextRef="i_2023-09-22_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-The2023EquityDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:EquitySalesAgreementMaximumValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">150.0</ix:nonFraction> million worth of its common stock, in amounts and at times to be determined by the Company.&#160;Sales of the Company&#8217;s common stock, if any, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be made in negotiated transactions or transactions that are deemed to be &#8220;at-the-market,&#8221; as defined in Rule&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">415</em> under the Securities Act, including sales made directly on the Nasdaq&#160;or similar securities exchange or sales made to or through a market maker other than on an exchange, at prices related to the prevailing market prices or at negotiated prices.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286772">not</span> sell shares of common stock under the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> Equity Distribution Agreement.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em>, the Company sold&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144286775" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-The2023EquityDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">404,305</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock under the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;Equity Distribution Agreement. For the same period, the Company received total accumulated net proceeds of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286777" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-The2023EquityDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfCommonStock" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, including&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286778" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-The2023EquityDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsOfStockIssuanceCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million of offering expenses, from these sales.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company generally uses net proceeds from these offerings to make investments, to pay down liabilities and for general corporate purposes. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, shares representing approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286779" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-The2023EquityDistributionAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:EquitySalesAgreementRemainingAmountAvailableForIssuance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">64.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of its common stock remain available for issuance and sale under the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;Equity Distribution Agreement.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="hrzn:StockRepurchaseProgramPolicyTextBlock" id="c144306658" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><b><i>Stock Repurchase Program</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 1, 2026,&#160;</em>the Board extended a previously authorized stock repurchase program which allows the Company to repurchase up to <em style="font: inherit;">$10.0</em> million of its common stock at prices below the Company&#8217;s net asset value per share as reported in its most recent consolidated financial statements, provided such purchases, in the aggregate, do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exceed <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> percent (<ix:nonFraction id="c144286785" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:StockRepurchaseProgramPercentageOfOutstandingStockMaximum" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2</ix:nonFraction>%) of the shares outstanding at the time of purchase and such shares are purchased only when the such shares are trading below <ix:nonFraction id="c144286786" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:StockRepurchaseProgramMaximumPercentageOfNetAssetValue" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">90</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company's most recently disclosed net asset value per share. Under the repurchase program, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may, </em>but is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> obligated to, repurchase shares of its outstanding common stock in the open market or in privately negotiated transactions from time to time. Any repurchases by the Company intends to&#160;comply with the requirements of Rule&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10b&#8209;18</em> under the Securities Exchange Act of <em style="font: inherit;">1934,</em> as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;), and any applicable requirements of the <em style="font: inherit;">1940</em> Act. Unless extended by the Board, the repurchase program will terminate on the earlier of <em style="font: inherit;"> June&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">30,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2027</em>&#160;or the repurchase of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286793" contextRef="i_2025-08-05" unitRef="USD" name="srt:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">10.0</ix:nonFraction> million of the Company&#8217;s common stock.&#160;During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, the Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286798"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286799">not</span></span> make any repurchases of its common stock under its stock repurchase program. From the date of the inception of the Company&#8217;s stock repurchase program through <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the Company repurchased <ix:nonFraction id="c144286800" contextRef="d_2021-04-24_2026-03-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">167,465</ix:nonFraction> shares of its common stock at an average price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286801" contextRef="d_2021-04-24_2026-03-31" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="hrzn:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodPerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.22</ix:nonFraction> on the open market at a total cost of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286802" contextRef="d_2021-04-24_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.9</ix:nonFraction> million. From time to time, the Board assesses the size and effectiveness of the stock repurchase program and could elect to increase or decrease the size of the program in the future.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsServicingOfFinancialAssetsPolicy" id="c144306659" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Transfers of financial assets</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Assets related to transactions that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the requirements under ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">860,</em> <i>Transfers and Servicing </i>for sale treatment under GAAP are reflected in the Company&#8217;s consolidated statements of assets and liabilities as investments. Those assets are owned by special purpose entities that are consolidated in the Company&#8217;s financial statements. The creditors of the special purpose entities have received security interests in such assets and such assets are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> intended to be available to the creditors of the Company (or any other affiliate of the Company).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Transfers of financial assets are accounted for as sales when control over the assets has been surrendered. Control over transferred assets is deemed to be surrendered when (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)&#160;the assets have been isolated from the Company&#160;&#8212; put presumptively beyond the reach of the transferor and its creditors, even in bankruptcy or other receivership, (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>)&#160;the transferee obtains the right (free of conditions that constrain it from taking advantage of that right) to pledge or exchange the transferred assets and (<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>)&#160;the transferor does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> maintain effective control over the transferred assets through either (a)&#160;an agreement that both entitles and obligates the transferor to repurchase or redeem the assets before maturity or (b)&#160;the ability to unilaterally cause the holder to return specific assets, other than through a cleanup call.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c144306660" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><b><i>Recently issued</i></b>&#160;<b><i>accounting pronouncement</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income - Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>). ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> requires disaggregated disclosure of certain costs and expenses, including purchase of inventory, employee compensation, depreciation, amortization and depletion, within relevant income statement captions. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> is effective for years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>Early adoption and retrospective application are permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> Related party transactions</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Investment Management Agreement</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">At a meeting of the stockholders convened on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 25, 2023&#160;</em>and reconvened on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 28, 2023</em><i>,</i>&#160;the Company&#8217;s stockholders, upon the recommendation of the Board, approved an investment management agreement with the Advisor, which became effective on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2023</em><i> </i>(the&#160;&#8220;Original Investment Management Agreement&#8221;).&#160;The Original Investment Management Agreement was&#160;effective for <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>&#160;years from the date of approval and then was required to be annually reapproved by the Board for a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-year period. The Original Investment Management Agreement was considered and reapproved by the Company&#8217;s Board, including a majority of the independent directors, on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 10, 2024 </em>for a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-year period.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025, </em>the Company entered into a new investment management agreement with the Advisor (the &#8220;New Investment Management Agreement&#8221;, collectively with the Original Investment Management Agreement, the &#8220;Investment Management Agreement&#8221;) in connection with the closing of a transaction pursuant to which Momentum US Bidco LLC, an affiliate of Wendel SE, acquired <ix:nonFraction id="c144286859" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LegalEntityAxis-MomentumUSBidcoLLCMember_OwnershipAxis-MonroeCapitalIntermediateHoldingsLLCMember_TypeOfArrangementAxis-EquityPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:OwnershipPercentageAcquired" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">75</ix:nonFraction>% of the outstanding equity interests of Monroe Capital Intermediate Holdings, LLC, the indirect parent company of the Advisor, and certain other affiliates of Monroe Capital LLC (the &#8220;Transaction&#8221;) (any such affiliate party to the Transaction, collectively, &#8220;Monroe&#8221;). The Transaction constituted a change of control in the Advisor and terminated the Original Investment Management Agreement. On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 10, 2024, </em>the Company&#8217;s Board, including a majority of the independent directors, approved, and recommended for approval by the Company&#8217;s stockholders, the New Investment Management Agreement. The New Investment Management Agreement was approved, subject to the closing of the Transaction, by the Company&#8217;s stockholders at a special meeting of stockholders held on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 21, 2025. </em>The terms of the New Investment Management Agreement, including the fee structure and services to be provided, are the same as the terms of the Original Investment Management Agreement, except for the date and term. Under the terms of the Investment Management Agreement, the Advisor determines the composition of the Company&#8217;s investment portfolio, the nature and timing of the changes to the investment portfolio and the manner of implementing such changes; identifies, evaluates and negotiates the structure of the investments the Company makes (including performing due diligence on the Company&#8217;s prospective portfolio companies); and closes, monitors and administers the investments the Company makes, including the exercise of any voting or consent rights.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Advisor&#8217;s services under the Investment Management Agreement are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exclusive to the Company, and the Advisor is free to furnish similar services to other entities so long as its services to the Company are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> impaired. The Advisor is a registered investment adviser with the SEC. The Advisor receives fees for providing services to the Company under the Investment Management Agreement, consisting of <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> components, a base management fee and an incentive fee.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The base management fee is&#160;calculated at an annual rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c144286863" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:BaseManagementFeeAnnualPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2.00</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s gross assets (less cash and cash equivalents) including any assets acquired with the proceeds of leverage; provided, that, to the extent the Company&#8217;s gross assets (less cash and cash equivalents) exceed <em style="font: inherit;">$250</em> million, the base management fee on the amount of such excess over <em style="font: inherit;">$250</em> million will be calculated at an annual rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c144286866" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:BaseManagementFeeAnnualPercentGrossAssetsExceeding250Million" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">1.60</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s gross assets (less cash and cash equivalents) including any assets acquired with the proceeds of leverage. The base management fee is payable&#160;monthly in arrears and is prorated for any partial&#160;month.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The base management fee payable at <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286867" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ManagementFeePayable" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million. The base management fee expense was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286869" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ManagementFeeExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286870" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ManagementFeeExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;for&#160;the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The incentive fee has <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> parts, as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> part, which is subject to the Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism, as defined below, is calculated and payable quarterly in arrears based on the Company&#8217;s Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income for the immediately preceding calendar quarter. For this purpose, &#8220;Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income&#8221; means interest income, dividend income and any other income (including any other fees (other than fees for providing managerial assistance), such as commitment, origination, structuring, diligence and consulting fees or other fees received from portfolio companies) accrued during the calendar quarter, minus expenses for the quarter (including the base management fee, expenses payable under the Administration Agreement (as defined below), and any interest expense and any dividends paid on any issued and outstanding preferred stock, but excluding the incentive fee). Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income includes, in the case of investments with a deferred interest feature (such as original issue discount, debt instruments with PIK interest and <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em> coupon securities), accrued income the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet received in cash. The incentive fee with respect to the Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income is <ix:nonFraction id="c144286877" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:IncentiveFeeToPreincentiveNetInvestmentIncome" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">20.00</ix:nonFraction>% of the amount, if any, by which the Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income for the immediately preceding calendar quarter exceeds a hurdle rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c144286878" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:PreincentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeHurdleRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">1.75</ix:nonFraction>% (which is <ix:nonFraction id="c144286879" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:PreincentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeHurdleRateAnnualized" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">7.00</ix:nonFraction>% annualized) of the Company&#8217;s net assets at the end of the immediately preceding calendar quarter, adjusted for any share issuances or repurchases during the relevant quarter, subject to a &#8220;catch-up&#8221; provision measured as of the end of each calendar quarter. Under this provision, in any calendar quarter, the Advisor receives <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> incentive fee until the Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income equals the hurdle rate of <em style="font: inherit;">1.75%,</em> but then receives, as a &#8220;catch-up,&#8221; <ix:nonFraction id="c144286882" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:PreincentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeCatchupPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100.00</ix:nonFraction>% of the Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income with respect to that portion of such Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income, if any, that exceeds the hurdle rate but is less than <ix:nonFraction id="c144286883" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:PreincentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeMaximumRateToTriggerCatchup" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="6">2.1875</ix:nonFraction>% quarterly (which is <ix:nonFraction id="c144286884" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:PreincentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeMaximumRateToTriggerCatchupAnnualized" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">8.75</ix:nonFraction>% annualized). The effect of this &#8220;catch-up&#8221; provision is that, if Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income exceeds <em style="font: inherit;">2.1875%</em> in any calendar quarter, the Advisor will receive <em style="font: inherit;">20.00%</em> of the Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income as if the hurdle rate did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> apply.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
