   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include any realized capital gains, realized capital losses or unrealized capital appreciation or depreciation. Because of the structure of the incentive fee, it is possible that the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>pay an incentive fee in a quarter in which the Company incurs a loss. For example, if the Company receives Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income in excess of the quarterly minimum hurdle rate, the Company will pay the applicable incentive fee up to the Incentive Fee Cap, defined below, even if the Company has incurred a loss in that quarter due to realized and unrealized capital losses. The Company&#8217;s net investment income used to calculate this part of the incentive fee is also included in the amount of the Company&#8217;s gross assets used to calculate the <em style="font: inherit;">2.00%</em> base management fee. These calculations are appropriately prorated for any period of less than <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months and adjusted for any share issuances or repurchases during the current quarter.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The incentive fee on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income is subject to a fee cap and deferral mechanism which is determined based upon a look-back period of up to <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;years and is expensed when incurred. For this purpose, the look-back period for the incentive fee based on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income (the &#8220;Incentive Fee Look-back Period&#8221;) includes the relevant calendar quarter and the <em style="font: inherit;">11</em> preceding full calendar quarters. Each quarterly incentive fee payable on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income is subject to a cap (the &#8220;Incentive Fee Cap&#8221;) and a deferral mechanism through which the Advisor <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>recoup a portion of such deferred incentive fees (collectively, the &#8220;Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism&#8221;). The Incentive Fee Cap is equal to (a)&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">20.00%</em> of Cumulative Pre-Incentive Fee Net Return (as defined below) during the Incentive Fee Look-back Period less (b)&#160;cumulative incentive fees of any kind paid to the Advisor during the Incentive Fee Look-back Period. To the extent the Incentive Fee Cap is <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em> or a negative value in any calendar quarter, the Company will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> pay an incentive fee on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income to the Advisor in that quarter. To the extent that the payment of incentive fees on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income is limited by the Incentive Fee Cap, the payment of such fees will be deferred and paid in subsequent calendar quarters up to <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;years after their date of deferment, subject to certain limitations, which are set forth in the Investment Management Agreement. The Company only pays incentive fees on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income to the extent allowed by the Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism. &#8220;Cumulative Pre-Incentive Fee Net Return&#8221; during any Incentive Fee Look-back Period means the sum of (a)&#160;Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income and the base management fee for each calendar quarter during the Incentive Fee Look-back Period and (b)&#160;the sum of cumulative realized capital gains and losses, cumulative unrealized capital appreciation and cumulative unrealized capital depreciation during the applicable Incentive Fee Look-back Period.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> part of the incentive fee is determined and payable in arrears as of the end of each calendar&#160;year (or, upon termination of the Investment Management Agreement, as of the termination date), and equals <em style="font: inherit;">20.00%</em> of the Company&#8217;s realized capital gains, if any, on a cumulative basis from the date of the election to be a BDC through the end of each calendar&#160;year, computed net of all realized capital losses and unrealized capital depreciation on a cumulative basis through the end of such&#160;year, less all previous amounts paid in respect of the capital gain incentive fee. However, in accordance with GAAP, the Company is required to include the aggregate unrealized capital appreciation on investments in the calculation and accrue a capital gain incentive fee on a quarterly basis, as if such unrealized capital appreciation were realized, even though such unrealized capital appreciation is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> permitted to be considered in calculating the fee actually payable under the Investment Management Agreement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The performance based incentive fee expense was $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286901" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncentiveFeeExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>. There was <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286903">no</span> performance based incentive fee expense for&#160;the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em>.&#160;The incentive fee on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income was subject to the Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, which&#160;resulted in $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286907" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:IncentiveFeeCapAndDeferralMechanismReductionToExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286908" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:IncentiveFeeCapAndDeferralMechanismReductionToExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.1</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively,&#160;of reduced expense and additional net investment income.&#160;This deferral represents a contingent future liability and is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> accrued until the amount can be reasonably estimated and payment is probable. The remaining deferred amount <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be paid up to <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> years after the date of deferment. The performance based incentive fee payable as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;was $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286911" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-InvestmentManagementAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncentiveFeePayable" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. There was <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286912">no</span> performance&#160;based incentive fee payable as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. The entire incentive fee payable as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;represented part <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of the incentive fee.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company&#8217;s Advisor agreed to waive the portion of its quarterly income incentive fee, if any, if and to the extent that, after payment of such portion, the Company&#8217;s net investment income per share for such quarter would be less than the quarterly distribution per share declared in such quarter. The income incentive fee waiver was&#160;effective commencing with the quarter ending <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025 </em>and terminated&#160;with the quarter ending <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.&#160;</em>During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em>, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286915">no</span>&#160;income incentive fee was earned.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -7pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Administration Agreement</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company entered into an administration agreement (the &#8220;Administration Agreement&#8221;) with the Advisor to provide administrative services to the Company. For providing these services, facilities and personnel, the Company reimburses the Advisor for the Company&#8217;s allocable portion of overhead and other expenses incurred by the Advisor in performing its obligations under the Administration Agreement, including rent, the fees and expenses associated with performing compliance functions and the Company&#8217;s allocable portion of the costs of compensation and related expenses of the Company&#8217;s Chief Financial Officer and Chief Compliance Officer and their respective staffs. The administrative fee expense was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286917" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-AdministrationAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AdministrativeFeesExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286918">$0.4</span>&#160;million for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively. The administrative fee payable at&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286921" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-AdministrationAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:AdministrativeFeesPayable" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144286922" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-AdministrationAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:AdministrativeFeesPayable" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively. The administrative fee payable is included in other accrued liabilities on the Company's Statement of Assets and Liabilities.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i><b>Advisory Fee Waiver</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In connection with entry into the Merger Agreement with MRCC, HMMS, Inc., a Maryland corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, Monroe Capital BDC Advisors, LLC, an investment adviser to MRCC, and the Advisor, the Advisor has agreed to waive $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286923" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-MergerAgreementFeeWaiverMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InvestmentCompanyContractualAndVoluntaryFeesWaived" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">4.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of base management fees and/or incentive fees (the &#8220;Fee Waiver&#8221;) due and payable to the Advisor pursuant to the terms of the Investment Management Agreement at the rate of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286924" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_TypeOfArrangementAxis-MergerAgreementFeeWaiverMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:BaseManagementAndIncentiveFeesAmountWaivedPerQuarter" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million per quarter commencing with the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> fiscal quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2026.</em> The Fee Waiver will be in effect until the end of the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> fiscal quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2027</em> and, for each applicable fiscal quarter, will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exceed the total amount of base management fees and incentive fees earned by the Advisor during such fiscal quarter.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Exemptive Relief</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The Advisor <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>provide the Company&#160;with an opportunity to co-invest with other investment vehicles managed by the&#160;Advisor, Monroe and/or their affiliates. Under the <em style="font: inherit;">1940</em> Act, absent receipt of exemptive relief from the SEC, the Company&#160;and its&#160;affiliates are precluded from co-investing in negotiated investments with other funds and accounts sponsored or managed by the&#160;Advisor, Monroe and their affiliates. Since <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2023, </em>the Company&#160;and its&#160;Advisor have&#160;relied on exemptive relief from the SEC granted to certain affiliates of Monroe on <em style="font: inherit;"> October 15, 2014, </em>as amended on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 10, 2023. </em>The exemptive relief affords the&#160;Advisor greater flexibility to negotiate the terms of co-investments if the&#160;Board determines that it would be advantageous for the Company&#160;to co-invest with other accounts sponsored or managed by the&#160;Advisor, Monroe or their affiliates in a manner consistent with the Company's&#160;investment objectives, positions, policies, strategies and restrictions as well as regulatory requirements and other pertinent factors. On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 14, 2025 </em>Monroe, et al. filed an application, and amendments to the application on <em style="font: inherit;"> August 6, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> October 3, 2025, </em>for a new exemptive relief order for co-investments for the Company, the Advisor, Monroe and its affiliates. On <em style="font: inherit;"> November 21, 2025, </em>a notice of the filing of the application was issued (Investment Company Act Release <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">35799</em>). On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 17, 2025, </em>the SEC granted an order for such exemptive relief (File <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">812</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">15798</em>). The Company is&#160;required to comply with all terms and conditions required therein.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 9pt;"><i><b>RoHo Capital Opportunity&#160;LLC</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 18, 2026, </em>the Company and CR Financial Holdings, Inc. (&#8220;CRFH&#8221;) entered into a limited liability company agreement (the &#8220;LLC Agreement&#8221;) to form a new joint venture, RoHo Capital Opportunity Fund LLC f/k/a HRZN CRFH LLC&#160;(the &#8220;Joint Venture&#8221;). The Joint Venture is intended to enhance the investment strategy of the Company by providing growth capital financing solutions to small and micro-cap public companies.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company has committed&#160;to invest up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286968" contextRef="i_2026-03-18_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-CrfhJointVentureMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:AmountCommittedToInvest" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">87.5</ix:nonFraction> million in the Joint Venture and CRFH has committed to invest up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c144286969" contextRef="i_2026-03-18_LegalEntityAxis-CrFinancialHoldingsMember_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-CrfhJointVentureMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:AmountCommittedToInvest" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">12.5</ix:nonFraction> million in the Joint Venture. Investments by each of the Company and CRFH in the Joint Venture will be made in the form of membership interests. All investments by the Joint Venture must be approved by the unanimous vote of the Joint Venture&#8217;s investment committee, which is comprised of an equal number of representatives designated by each of the Company and CRFH. Further, all other decisions regarding the management of the Joint Venture require the approval of the majority of the Joint Venture&#8217;s board of directors, which is comprised of an equal number of representatives from each of the Company and CRFH.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144286970">no</span> commitments were funded into the Joint Venture and <em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;investments were made by the Joint Venture.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">A controlled affiliated company is generally a portfolio company in which the Company owns more than <em style="font: inherit;">25%</em> of such portfolio company&#8217;s voting securities or has the power to exercise control over management or policies of such portfolio company (including through a management agreement).</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>Note</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">6.</em> Fair value</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">Prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> July 30, 2022, </em>the Board determined the fair value of the Company&#8217;s investments. Pursuant to the amended SEC Rule <em style="font: inherit;">2a</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">5</em> of the <em style="font: inherit;">1940</em> Act, on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 29, 2022, </em>the Board designated the Advisor as the Company&#8217;s &#8220;valuation designee.&#8221; The Board is responsible for oversight of the valuation designee. The valuation designee has established a Valuation Committee to determine in good faith the fair value of the Company&#8217;s investments, based on input from&#160;the Advisor&#8217;s management and personnel and independent valuation firms which are engaged at the direction of the Valuation Committee to assist in the valuation of certain portfolio investments lacking a readily available market quotation at least once during a trailing <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em>-month period. The Valuation Committee determines fair values pursuant to a valuation policy approved by the Board and pursuant to a consistently applied valuation process. This valuation process is conducted at the end of each fiscal quarter, with at least <ix:nonFraction id="c144287353" contextRef="i_2022-06-30_MeasurementInputTypeAxis-MeasurementInputHypotheticalMarketYieldsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentMeasurementInput" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction>% (based on fair value) of the Company&#8217;s valuation of portfolio companies lacking readily available market quotations subject to review by an independent valuation firm.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company uses fair value measurements made by the valuation designee to record fair value adjustments to certain assets and liabilities and to determine fair value disclosures. Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Fair value is best determined based upon quoted market prices. However, in certain instances, there are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> quoted market prices for certain assets or liabilities. In cases where quoted market prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are based on estimates using present value or other valuation techniques. Those techniques are significantly affected by the assumptions used, including the discount rate and estimates of future cash flows. Accordingly, the fair value estimates <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized in an immediate settlement of the asset or liability.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Fair value measurements focus on exit prices in an orderly transaction (that is, <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a forced liquidation or distressed sale) between market participants at the measurement date under current market conditions. If there has been a significant decrease in the volume and level of activity for the asset or liability, a change in valuation technique or the use of multiple valuation techniques <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be appropriate. In such instances, determining the price at which willing market participants would transact at the measurement date under current market conditions depends on the facts and circumstances and requires the use of significant judgment.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company&#8217;s fair value measurements are classified into a fair value hierarchy in accordance with ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820,</em> <i>Fair Value Measurement</i>, based on the markets in which the assets and liabilities are traded and the reliability of the assumptions used to determine fair value. The <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> categories within the hierarchy are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 45pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets and liabilities.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 45pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Observable inputs other than Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> prices such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active, and model-based valuation techniques for which all significant inputs are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the assets or liabilities.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 45pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Unobservable inputs that are supported by little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market activity and that are significant to the fair value of the assets or liabilities. Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> assets and liabilities include financial instruments whose value is determined using pricing models, discounted cash flow methodologies or similar techniques, as well as instruments for which the determination of fair value requires significant management judgment or estimation.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Due to the inherent uncertainty of determining the fair value of investments that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a readily available market value, the fair value of the Company&#8217;s investments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>fluctuate from period to period. Additionally, the fair value of the Company&#8217;s investments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>differ significantly from the values that would have been used had a ready market existed for such investments and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>differ materially from the values that the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>ultimately realize. Further, such investments are generally subject to legal and other restrictions on resale or otherwise are less liquid than publicly traded securities. If the Company was required to liquidate a portfolio investment in a forced or liquidation sale, the Company could realize significantly less than the value at which the Company has recorded such portfolio investment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Cash:</i> The carrying amount is a reasonable estimate of fair value. These financial instruments are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recorded at fair value on a recurring basis and are categorized as Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> within the fair value hierarchy described above.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Money market funds:</i>&#160;&#160;The carrying amounts are valued at their net asset value as of the close of business on the day of valuation. These financial instruments are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis and are categorized as Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>&#160;within the fair value hierarchy described above as these funds can be redeemed daily.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Debt investments:</i> The fair value of debt investments is estimated by discounting the expected future cash flows using the period end rates at which similar debt investments would be made to borrowers with similar credit ratings and for the same remaining maturities. Significant increases (decreases) in this unobservable input would result in a significantly lower (higher) fair value measurement. These assets are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis and are categorized as Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> within the fair value hierarchy described above.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Under certain circumstances, the Company&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>use an alternative technique to value debt investments that better reflects its&#160;fair value such as the use of multiple probability weighted cash flow models when the expected future cash flows contain elements of variability.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Warrant investments:</i> The Company values its&#160;warrants using the Black-Scholes valuation model incorporating the following material assumptions:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Underlying asset value of the issuer is estimated based on information available, including any information regarding the most recent rounds of borrower funding. Significant increases (decreases) in this unobservable input would result in a significantly higher (lower) fair value measurement.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Volatility, or the amount of uncertainty or risk about the size of the changes in the warrant price, is based on indices of publicly traded companies similar in nature to the underlying company issuing the warrant. A total of <em style="font: inherit;">seven</em> such indices are used. Significant increases (decreases) in this unobservable input would result in a significantly higher (lower) fair value measurement.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The risk-free interest rates are derived from the U.S. Treasury yield curve. The risk-free interest rates are calculated based on a weighted average of the risk-free interest rates that correspond closest to the expected remaining life of the warrant.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Other adjustments, including a marketability discount on private company warrants, are estimated based on management&#8217;s judgment about the general industry environment.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Historical portfolio experience on cancellations and exercises of the Company&#8217;s warrants are utilized as the basis for determining the estimated time to exit of the warrants in each financial reporting period. Warrants <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be exercised in the event of acquisitions, mergers or initial public offerings, and cancelled due to events such as bankruptcies, restructuring activities or additional financings. These events cause the expected remaining life assumption to be shorter than the contractual term of the warrants. Significant increases (decreases) in this unobservable input would result in significantly higher (lower) fair value measurement.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Under certain circumstances the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>use an alternative technique to value warrants that better reflects the warrants&#8217; fair value, such as an expected settlement of a warrant in the near term or a model that incorporates a put feature associated with the warrant. The fair value <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be determined based on the expected proceeds to be received from such settlement or based on the net present value of the expected proceeds from the put option.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The fair value of the Company&#8217;s warrants held in publicly traded companies is determined based on inputs that are readily available in public markets or can be derived from information available in public markets. Therefore, the Company has categorized these warrants as Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> within the fair value hierarchy described above. The fair value of the Company&#8217;s warrants held in private companies is determined using both observable and unobservable inputs and represents management&#8217;s best estimate of what market participants would use in pricing the warrants at the measurement date. Therefore, the Company has categorized these warrants as Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> within the fair value hierarchy described above. These assets are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Equity investments:</i> The fair value of an equity investment in a privately held company is initially the face value of the amount invested. The Company adjusts the fair value of equity investments in private companies upon the completion of a new <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party round of equity financing. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>make adjustments to fair value, absent a new equity financing event, based upon positive or negative changes in a portfolio company&#8217;s financial or operational performance. Significant increases (decreases) in this unobservable input would result in a significantly higher (lower) fair value measurement. The Company has categorized these equity investments as Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> within the fair value hierarchy described above. The fair value of an equity investment in a publicly traded company is based upon the closing public share price on the date of measurement. Therefore, the Company has categorized these equity investments as Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> within the fair value hierarchy described above. These assets are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Other investments: </i>Other investments are valued based on the facts and circumstances of the underlying contractual agreement. The Company currently values these contractual agreements using a multiple probability weighted cash flow model as the contractual future cash flows contain elements of variability. Significant changes in the estimated cash flows and probability weightings would result in a significantly higher or lower fair value measurement. The Company has categorized these other investments as Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> within the fair value hierarchy described above. These other investments are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Transfers between levels are recognized&#160;as of the date of the event or change in circumstances that caused the transfer, based on changes in the observability or significance of valuation inputs.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The following tables detail the assets that are carried at fair value and measured at fair value on a recurring basis as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and indicate the fair value hierarchy of the valuation techniques utilized by the Company to determine the fair value:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Borrowings:</i> The Credit Facilities approximate fair value due to the variable interest rate of the facilities and are categorized as Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> within the fair value hierarchy described above. Additionally, the Company considers its creditworthiness in determining the fair value of such borrowings. The fair value of the fixed-rate <em style="font: inherit;">2027</em> Notes (as defined in Note <em style="font: inherit;">7</em>) is based on the closing public share price on the date of measurement. On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the closing price of the <em style="font: inherit;">2027</em> Notes on the New York Stock Exchange was <em style="font: inherit;">$<ix:nonFraction id="c144287398" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2026NotesMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="hrzn:DebtInstrumentSharePrice" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">24.59</ix:nonFraction></em>&#160;per note, and the <em style="font: inherit;">2027</em> Notes had an aggregate fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144287401" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2026NotesMember_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel1Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">56.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. Therefore, the Company has categorized this&#160;borrowing as Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> within the fair value hierarchy described above. Based on market yields on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the fair value of the <em style="font: inherit;">2028</em> Notes&#160;(as defined in Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">7</em>) was $<ix:nonFraction id="c144287405" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2028NotesMember_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel3Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">57.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;and&#160;are&#160;categorized as Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;within the fair value hierarchy described above. Based on market yields on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the fair value of the <em style="font: inherit;">2031</em> Convertible&#160;Notes&#160;(as defined in Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">7</em>) was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144287409" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2031ConvertibleNotesMember_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel3Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.7</ix:nonFraction> million, and the <em style="font: inherit;">2031</em> Convertible Notes are&#160;categorized as Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;within the fair value hierarchy described above. Based on market yields on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the fair value of the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible&#160;Notes&#160;(as defined in Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">7</em>) was $<ix:nonFraction id="c144287414" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel3Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">16.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, and the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Notes are&#160;categorized as Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;within the fair value hierarchy described above. These borrowings are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recorded at fair value on a recurring basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Off-balance-sheet instruments:</i> Fair values for off-balance-sheet lending commitments are based on fees currently charged to enter into similar agreements, taking into account the remaining terms of the agreements and the counterparties&#8217; credit standings. Therefore, the Company has categorized these instruments as Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> within the fair value hierarchy described above.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company discloses fair value information about financial instruments, whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognized in the consolidated statement of assets and liabilities, for which it is practicable to estimate that value. Certain financial instruments are excluded from the disclosure requirements. Accordingly, the aggregate fair value amounts presented do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> represent the underlying value of the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The fair value amounts have been measured as of the reporting date and have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been reevaluated or updated for purposes of these financial statements subsequent to that date. As such, the fair values of these financial instruments subsequent to the reporting date <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be different than amounts reported.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, all of the balances of all the Company&#8217;s financial instruments were recorded at fair value, except for the Company&#8217;s borrowings, as previously described.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Market risk</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company assumes interest rate risk (the risk that general interest rate levels will change) as a result of its normal operations. As a result, the fair values of the Company&#8217;s financial instruments <em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>change when interest rate levels change, and that change <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be either favorable or unfavorable to the Company. Management attempts to match maturities of assets and liabilities to the extent believed necessary to minimize interest rate risk. Management monitors rates and maturities of assets and liabilities and attempts to minimize interest rate risk by adjusting terms of new debt investments and by investing in securities with terms that mitigate the Company&#8217;s overall interest rate risk.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Key Facility</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company entered into the Key Facility with Key effective <em style="font: inherit;"> November&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">4,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2013.</em> On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 26, 2026, </em>the Company amended the Key Facility, among other things, (i) to make Michael P. Balkin and&#160;Paul G. Seitz each an&#160;&#8220;Authorized Person&#8221;, (ii) to amend certain requirements to make a debt investment eligible for the borrowing base and (ii)&#160;to amend certain concentration limits. On <em style="font: inherit;"> June 20, 2024, </em>the Company amended the Key Facility, among other things, (i) to extend the date on which the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>request advances under the Key Facility to <em style="font: inherit;"> June 20, 2027 </em>and to extend the maturity date to <em style="font: inherit;"> June 20, 2029 </em>and (ii) to amend the interest rate to be based on the rate of interest published in The Wall Street Journal as the prime rate in the United States plus <ix:nonFraction id="c144287830" contextRef="d_2026-02-26_2026-02-26_DebtInstrumentAxis-KeyFacilityMember_VariableRateAxis-PrimeRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">0.10</ix:nonFraction>%, with an interest&#160;rate floor of <ix:nonFraction id="c144287831" contextRef="d_2026-04-26_2026-04-26_DebtInstrumentAxis-KeyFacilityMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember_VariableRateAxis-PrimeRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">4.10</ix:nonFraction>%. Prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> June 20, 2024, </em>the interest rate on the Key Facility was based on Prime plus <ix:nonFraction id="c144287832" contextRef="d_2024-06-19_2024-06-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-KeyFacilityMember_VariableRateAxis-PrimeRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">0.25</ix:nonFraction>%, with a prime rate floor of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144287833" contextRef="d_2024-06-19_2024-06-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-KeyFacilityMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember_VariableRateAxis-PrimeRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">4.25</ix:nonFraction>%. On <em style="font: inherit;"> June 29, 2023, </em>the Company amended the Key Facility, among other things, to increase the commitment amount to $<ix:nonFraction id="c144287834" contextRef="i_2023-06-29_DebtInstrumentAxis-KeyFacilityMember" unitRef="USD" name="hrzn:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacityAccordianFeature" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">150</ix:nonFraction> million and to increase the amount of the accordion feature which now allows for the potential increase in the total commitment amount to $<ix:nonFraction id="c144287835" contextRef="i_2023-06-29_DebtInstrumentAxis-KeyFacilityMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">300</ix:nonFraction> million. The Key Facility is collateralized by all debt investments and warrants held by Credit II and permits an advance rate of up to <ix:nonFraction id="c144287836" contextRef="i_2023-06-29_DebtInstrumentAxis-KeyFacilityMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:LineOfCreditFacilityAdvanceRateOfEligibleDebtInvestments" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">60</ix:nonFraction>% of eligible debt investments held by Credit II. The <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes had&#160;a stated maturity of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 30, 2026 </em>and could have been redeemed in whole or in part at the Company&#8217;s option at any time or from time to time on or after <em style="font: inherit;"> March 30, 2023 </em>at a redemption price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144287892" contextRef="i_2021-03-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2026NotesUnderwriterOptionMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleConversionPrice1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">25</ix:nonFraction> per security plus accrued and unpaid interest. The <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes bore&#160;interest at a rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c144287894" contextRef="i_2021-03-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2026NotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">4.875</ix:nonFraction>% per year, payable quarterly on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 30, </em><em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, </em><em style="font: inherit;"> September 30 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 30 </em>of each year. The <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes were the Company&#8217;s direct unsecured obligations and (i) ranked equally in right of payment with the Company&#8217;s current and future unsecured indebtedness; (ii) were senior in right of payment to any of the Company&#8217;s future indebtedness that expressly provides it is subordinated to the <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes; (iii) were effectively subordinated to all of the Company&#8217;s existing and future secured indebtedness (including indebtedness that is initially unsecured to which the Company subsequently grants security), to the extent of the value of the assets securing such indebtedness, and (iv) were structurally subordinated to all existing and future indebtedness and other obligations of any of the Company&#8217;s subsidiaries. The <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes were listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol &#8220;HTFB&#8221;.&#160;On <em style="font: inherit;"> January 28, 2026, </em>the Company&#160;redeemed all of the outstanding principal balance of the <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes plus accrued interest. The Company accelerated $<ix:nonFraction id="c144287899" contextRef="d_2026-01-28_2026-01-28_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2026NotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GainsLossesOnExtinguishmentOfDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of unamortized debt issuance costs related to the <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 4, 2025, </em>the Company&#160;entered into a note purchase agreement&#160;(the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2030</em> Note Purchase Agreement&#8221;), by and among the Company&#160;and&#160;each purchaser named therein, in connection with the issuance and sale of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144287939" contextRef="i_2025-09-04_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">40.0</ix:nonFraction> million aggregate principal of the Company&#8217;s <ix:nonFraction id="c144287940" contextRef="i_2025-09-04_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">5.50</ix:nonFraction>% convertible notes due <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em> (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2030</em> Convertible Notes&#8221;) in a&#160;transaction&#160;exempt from registration pursuant to Section <em style="font: inherit;">4</em>(a)(<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) of the Securities Act of <em style="font: inherit;">1933,</em> as amended. The Company&#160;received net proceeds (before expenses) from the sale of the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em> Convertible Notes of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c144287947" contextRef="d_2025-09-04_2025-09-04_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromConvertibleDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">36.6</ix:nonFraction> million.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Notes mature on <em style="font: inherit;"> <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-09-04_2025-09-04_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentMaturityDate" id="c144288062" format="ixt:date-monthname-day-year-en">September 4, 2030</ix:nonNumeric>, </em>unless earlier converted or repurchased in accordance with their terms.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Notes are direct unsecured obligations of the Company and rank (i) equal in right of payment to the Company&#8217;s existing and future unsecured indebtedness that is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subordinated in right of payment to the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Notes; (ii) senior in right of payment to the Company&#8217;s future indebtedness that is expressly subordinated in right of payment to the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Notes; (iii) effectively junior in right of payment to the Company&#8217;s existing and future secured indebtedness (including unsecured indebtedness that the Company later secures) to the extent of the value of the assets securing such indebtedness; and (iv) structurally junior to all existing and future indebtedness and other obligations of any of the Company&#8217;s subsidiaries. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> sinking fund is provided for the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Notes.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">At any time on or after <em style="font: inherit;"> October 4, 2025, </em>at the Company&#8217;s&#160;sole option, the Company&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>redeem, from time to time, the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Notes in whole or in part, out of funds legally available for such redemption, at <ix:nonFraction id="c144287958" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentRedemptionPricePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the principal amount prepaid plus accrued but unpaid interest to but excluding the date of prepayment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">Each holder of a <em style="font: style="font: inherit;"> October 4, 2025 </em>and prior to the close of business on the business day immediately preceding the maturity date, once or more times per calendar month, into such number of shares of common stock of the Company equal to the principal balance of the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Note being converted on the conversion date plus the accrued but unpaid interest on the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Note as of the conversion date, divided by the greater of (i) volume-weighted average closing sale price for the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144287963">five</span> trading days immediately prior to the relevant conversion date, or (ii) the Company&#8217;s most recently reported net asset value (&#8220;NAV&#8221;) per share immediately prior to the date of the notice of such exercise.&#160;If the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Notes were converted as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c144287965" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleNumberOfEquityInstruments" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,356,734</ix:nonFraction> shares would have been issued based on the Company&#8217;s most recently reported NAV per share immediately prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144287966" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleConversionPrice1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">6.98</ix:nonFraction>. The last reported price for the Company&#8217;s common stock on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144287967" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:SharePrice" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">4.21</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per share.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;"><em style="font: inherit;">No</em> holder of <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Notes <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>exercise its conversion right if upon conversion the holder would receive shares that would cause funds and accounts managed by the investment adviser to such funds and accounts and any person controlled by the parent company of such investment adviser to beneficially own in the aggregate more than <ix:nonFraction id="c144287970" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hrzn:DebtInstrumentConvertibleMaximumBeneficialOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">4.99</ix:nonFraction>% of the shares outstanding at such time.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Notes are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> listed on any exchange and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be transferred without the consent of the Company.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:FinancialInstrumentsDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3175331" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">8.</em> Financial instruments with off-balance-sheet risk</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In the normal course of business, the Company is party to financial instruments with off-balance-sheet risk to meet the financing needs of its borrowers. These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit and involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit risk in excess of the amount recognized in the consolidated statement of assets and liabilities. The Company attempts to limit its credit risk by conducting extensive due diligence and obtaining collateral where appropriate.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The balance of unfunded commitments to extend credit was $<ix:nonFraction id="c144288161" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-CommitmentsToExtendCreditMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OtherCommitment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">155.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c144288162" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-CommitmentsToExtendCreditMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OtherCommitment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">104.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, respectively. Commitments to extend credit consist principally of the unused portions of commitments that obligate the Company to extend credit, often subject to financial or non-financial milestones and other conditions to borrow that must be achieved before the commitment can be drawn. In addition, the commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses. Since commitments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>expire without being drawn upon, the total commitment amounts do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily represent future cash requirements.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">9.</em> Concentrations of credit risk</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company&#8217;s debt investments consist primarily of loans to development-stage companies at various stages of development in the technology, life science, healthcare information and services and sustainability industries. Many of these companies <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have relatively limited operating histories and also <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>experience variation in operating results. Many of these companies conduct business in regulated industries and could be affected by changes in government regulations. Most of the Company&#8217;s borrowers will need additional capital to satisfy their continuing working capital needs and other requirements, and in many instances, to service the interest and principal payments on the loans.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In certain circumstances, the Convertible Notes <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be convertible into cash or shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock, which can be dilutive to common stockholders. Diluted&#160;earnings (loss) available to each share of common stock outstanding during the reporting period included any additional shares of common stock that would be issued if all potentially dilutive securities were exercised. In accordance with ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">06,</em> the Company is required to disclose diluted EPS using the if-converted method that assumes conversion of convertible securities at the beginning of the reporting period or at the issuance date and is intended to show the maximum dilution effect to common stockholders regardless of how the conversion can occur. The&#160;Convertible Notes convert at the greater of (i) volume-weighted average closing sale price for the <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> trading days immediately prior to the relevant conversion date, or (ii) the Company&#8217;s most recently reported NAV per share immediately prior to the date of exercise. For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, using the if-converted method, the <em style="font: inherit;">2031</em> Convertible Notes would convert&#160;at the Company&#8217;s most recently reported NAV per share immediately prior to the beginning of the period, or&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144288445" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2031ConvertibleNotesMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleStockPriceTrigger" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">7.12</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per share.&#160;For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em>, using the if-converted method, the <em style="font: inherit;">2031</em> Convertible Notes would convert at the volume-weighted average closing sale price for the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144288448">five</span> trading days immediately prior to the beginning of the period, or $<ix:nonFraction id="c144288449" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleStockPriceTrigger" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">8.94</ix:nonFraction> per share. For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, using the if-converted method, the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em>&#160;Convertible Notes would convert&#160;at the Company&#8217;s most recently reported NAV per share immediately prior to the beginning of the period, or $<ix:nonFraction id="c144288452" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2030ConvertibleNotesMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleStockPriceTrigger" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">7.12</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per share. For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, the impact of the hypothetical conversion of the Convertible Notes would have been antidilutive because interest net of tax and nondiscretionary adjustments per common share obtainable on conversion exceeded basic EPS.</p>
