  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Overview</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">We are a specialty finance company that lends to and invests in development-stage companies in the technology, life science, healthcare information and services and sustainability industries, which we refer to as our &#8220;Target Industries.&#8221; Our investment objective is to maximize our investment portfolio&#8217;s total return by generating current income from the debt investments we make and capital appreciation from the warrants we receive when making such debt investments. We are focused on making secured debt investments, which we refer to collectively as &#8220;Venture Loans,&#8221; to venture capital and private equity backed companies and publicly traded companies in our Target Industries, which we refer to as &#8220;Venture Lending.&#8221; Our debt investments are typically secured by first liens or first liens behind a secured revolving line of credit, or collectively &#8220;Senior Term Loans.&#8221; Some of our debt investments may also be subordinated to term debt provided by third parties. As of March 31, 2026, 97.5%, or $629.3&#160;million, of our debt investment portfolio at fair value consisted of Senior Term Loans. Venture Lending is typically characterized by (1)&#160;the making of a secured debt investment after a venture capital or equity investment in the portfolio company has been made, which investment provides a source of cash to fund the portfolio company&#8217;s debt service obligations under the Venture Loan, (2)&#160;the senior priority of the Venture Loan which requires repayment of the Venture Loan prior to the equity investors realizing a return on their capital, (3)&#160;the amortization of the Venture Loan and (4)&#160;the lender&#8217;s receipt of warrants or other success fees with the making of the Venture Loan.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">We are an externally managed, closed-end, non-diversified management investment company that has elected to be regulated as a&#160;BDC&#160;under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended, or the 1940 Act. In addition, for U.S. federal income tax purposes, we have elected to be treated as a RIC&#160;under Subchapter M of the Code. As a BDC, we are required to comply with regulatory requirements, including limitations on our use of debt. We are permitted to, and expect to, finance our investments through borrowings subject to a 150% asset coverage test. As defined in the 1940 Act, asset coverage of 150% means that for every $100 of net assets a BDC holds, it may raise up to $200 from borrowing and issuing senior securities. The amount of leverage that we may employ will depend on our assessment of market conditions and other factors at the time of any proposed borrowing. As a RIC, we generally are not subject to corporate-level income taxes on our investment company taxable income, determined without regard to any deductions for dividends paid, and our net capital gain that we distribute as dividends for U.S. federal income tax purposes to our stockholders as long as we meet certain source-of-income, distribution, asset diversification and other requirements.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Debt investment asset quality</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">We use an internal credit rating system which rates each debt investment on a scale of 4 to 1, with 4 being the highest credit quality rating and 3 being the rating for a standard level of risk. A rating of 2 represents an increased level of risk and, while no loss is currently anticipated for a 2&#8209;rated debt investment, there is potential for future loss of principal. A rating of 1 represents a deteriorating credit quality and a high degree of risk of loss of principal. Our internal credit rating system is not a national credit rating system. As of March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, our debt investments had a weighted average credit rating of&#160;3.0&#160;and 2.9, respectively.&#160;The following table shows the classification of our debt investment portfolio by credit rating as of March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025:</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Net increase (decrease) in net assets resulting from operations can vary substantially from period to period for various reasons, including, without limitation, the recognition of realized gains and losses and unrealized appreciation and depreciation on investments. As a result, quarterly comparisons of net increase in net assets resulting from operations may not be meaningful.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Investment income</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Total investment income&#160;decreased&#160;by&#160;$0.4&#160;million, or 1.8%, to $24.1&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;as compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025. For the three months ended March 31, 2026, total investment income consisted primarily of (1)&#160;$23.1&#160;million in interest income from investments, which included $5.0&#160;million in income from the accretion of origination fees and end of term payments&#160;and&#160;$1.3&#160;million in PIK interest income and (2)&#160;$1.0&#160;million in fee income.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Interest income on debt investments decreased&#160;by $0.4&#160;million, or 1.6%, to $23.1&#160;million, for the three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;compared to the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2025. Interest income on debt investments for the three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;as compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025 decreased primarily due to a decrease in the Prime Rate which is the base rate for most of our variable rate debt investments and&#160;a decrease of&#160;$19.5 million, or 3.0%, in our average earning debt investments partially offset by an increase in accelerated income from prepayments.&#160;The proportion of&#160;total investment income that resulted from the portion of ETPs not received in cash for the three months ended&#160;March 31, 2026 and 2025 was&#160;6.0%&#160;and 4.6%, respectively.&#160;The&#160;increase&#160;in the proportion of total investment income that resulted from the portion of ETPs not received in cash was a result of an increase in accretion of final payments&#160;for the three months ended March 31, 2026 compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">PIK interest income&#160;increased&#160;by&#160;$1.0&#160;million, or 348.4%, to&#160;$1.3&#160;million for the three&#160;months ended March 31, 2026&#160;compared to the three months ended&#160;&#160;March 31, 2025. For the three&#160;months ended&#160;March 31, 2026 and 2025,&#160;5.3%&#160;and 1.2%, respectively, of total investment income was attributable to non-cash PIK interest income. The increase&#160;in PIK interest income as a percentage of total investment income was primarily&#160;due to&#160;an&#160;increase&#160;in earning assets that contain a PIK feature for the three months ended March 31, 2026 compared to the three&#160;months ended March 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Fee income, which includes success fee, other fee and prepayment fee income on debt investments, decreased&#160;by $0.1&#160;million, or 6.1%, to $1.0&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025 primarily due to a lower&#160;success fee and other fee income&#160;for the&#160;three months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Expenses</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Total expenses increased&#160;by&#160;$1.4&#160;million, or 10.6%, to&#160;$14.8&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;as compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025. Total expenses for each period consisted of interest expense, base management fee, incentive and administrative fees, professional fees and general and administrative expenses.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Interest expense decreased&#160;by&#160;$0.5&#160;million, or 5.8%, to $8.2&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2026 as compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025. Interest expense, which includes the amortization of debt issuance costs, decreased primarily due to&#160;a decrease&#160;in average borrowings&#160;for the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026 of $25.3&#160;million, or 5.4%, &#160;as compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025&#160;and a decrease&#160;in our effective cost of debt for the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026 as compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Base management fee expense decreased&#160;by&#160;$0.1&#160;million, or 1.9%, to $3.1&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;as compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025. Base management fee decreased&#160;primarily due to&#160;a decrease&#160;of&#160;$15.0&#160;million, or 2.1%,&#160;in average gross assets less cash for the three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;as compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">P</span>erformance based incentive fee expense&#160;increased&#160;by $1.8&#160;million to&#160;$1.8&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;as compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025.&#160;There was no performance based incentive fee expense for three months ended March 31, 2025.&#160;This&#160;increase was due to an&#160;Incentive Fee Cap calculated based on the Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism in our Investment Management Agreement of $0.4&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2026 compared to an Incentive Fee Cap of $2.1&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2025.&#160;The Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism resulted in $0.4 million and $2.1&#160;million of reduced incentive fee expense and increased net investment income for the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The incentive fee on pre-incentive fee net investment income was subject to the Incentive Fee Cap for the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026&#160;due to the cumulative incentive fees paid exceeding 20% of cumulative pre-incentive fee net return during the applicable quarter and the 11 preceding full calendar quarters.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Net realized gains and losses and net unrealized appreciation and depreciation</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Realized gains or losses on investments are measured by the difference between the net proceeds from the repayment or sale and the cost basis of our investments without regard to unrealized appreciation or depreciation previously recognized. Realized gains or losses on investments include investments charged off during the period, net of recoveries. The net unrealized appreciation or depreciation on investments primarily reflects the change in portfolio investment fair values during the reporting period, including the reversal of previously recorded unrealized appreciation or depreciation when gains or losses are realized.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">During the three months ended </span>March 31, 2026<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;and &#160;</span>March 31, 2025<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">, we realized net </span>losses<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;on investments totaling&#160;</span>$0.2<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;million and&#160;</span>$0.001<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> million, respectively. During the three months ended </span>March 31, 2026<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">, we converted </span>$15.1<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;million in outstanding principal of the 2030&#160;Convertible Notes (as defined below) which resulted in a realized loss on extinguishment of debt of $1.3</span><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;million. During the same period, we r</span>edeemed all of the outstanding principal balance of the 2026 Notes (as defined below) which resulted in a realized loss on <span style="background-color:#ffffff">extinguishment of debt of&#160;$0.1&#160;</span><span style="background-color:#ffffff">million.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">During the three months ended March 31, 2026, net unrealized depreciation&#160;on investments totaled&#160;$4.6&#160;million which was primarily due to the unrealized depreciation on two of our deb<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">t investments and one of our equity investments&#160;and the unrealized depreciation on our warrant investments</span>. During the three months ended March 31, 2025, net unrealized depreciation on investments totaled&#160;$32.2 million which was primarily due to the unrealized depreciation on three of our debt investments and two of our equity investments.&#160;The difficult equity fundraising market and under performance of certain portfolio companies, among other factors, resulted in our reduction of the fair market value of the debt investments in such portfolio companies, thus increasing the unrealized depreciation on such debt investments.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><b><i>Liquidity and capital resources</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">As of March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, we had cash and investments in money market funds of $70.6&#160;million and $140.2 million, respectively. Cash and investments in money market funds are available to fund new investments, reduce borrowings, pay expenses, repurchase common stock and pay distributions. In addition, as of March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, we had $2.6&#160;million and $2.5&#160;million, respectively, of restricted investments in money market funds. Restricted investments in money market funds may be used to make monthly interest and principal payments on our&#160;NYL Facility or our Nuveen Facility. Our primary sources of capital have been from our public&#160;equity offerings, use of our revolving credit facility (the &#8220;Key Facility&#8221;) with KeyBank National Association (&#8220;Key&#8221;),&#160;the Note Funding Agreement (the &#8220;NYL Facility&#8221;), with several entities owned or affiliated with New York Life Insurance Company and the Nuveen Note Funding Agreement (the &#8220;Nuveen Facility&#8221;,&#160;together with the Key Facility and the NYL Facility,&#160;the &#8220;Credit Facilities&#8221;) with several entities owned or affiliated with Nuveen Alternative Advisors LLC,&#160;and issuance of our public and private debt securities.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">On September 22, 2023, we entered into an At-The-Market (or &#8220;ATM&#8221;) sales agreement (or the &#8220;2023&#160;Equity Distribution Agreement&#8221;) with Goldman Sachs&#160;&amp; Co. LLC and B. Riley FBR,&#160;Inc., (each a &#8220;Sales Agent&#8221; and, collectively, the &#8220;Sales Agents&#8221;). The 2023 Equity Distribution Agreement provides that we may offer and sell shares of our common stock from time to time through the Sales Agents up to $150.0 million worth of our common stock, in amounts and at times to be determined by us.&#160;Sales of our common stock, if any, may be made in negotiated transactions or transactions that are deemed to be &#8220;at-the-market,&#8221; as defined in Rule 415 under the Securities Act, including sales made directly on the NASDAQ or similar securities exchange or sales made to or through a market maker other than on an exchange, at prices related to the prevailing market prices or at negotiated prices.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">During the three months ended March 31, 2026, we did not sell any shares of common stock under the 2023 Equity Distribution Agreement.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">During the three months ended March 31, 2025, we&#160;sold&#160;404,305 shares of common stock under the 2023&#160;Equity Distribution Agreement. For the same period, we&#160;received total accumulated net proceeds of approximately $3.6&#160;million, including&#160;$0.1 million of offering expenses, from these sales.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">On May 1, 2026, our Board extended a previously authorized stock repurchase program which allows us to repurchase up to $10.0 million of our common stock at prices below our net asset value (&#8220;NAV&#8221;) per share as reported in our most recent consolidated financial statements, provided such purchases, in the aggregate, do not exceed two percent (2%) of the shares outstanding at the time of purchase and such shares are purchased only when the such shares are trading below 90% of our&#160;most recently disclosed NAV per share. Under the repurchase program, we may, but are not obligated to, repurchase shares of our outstanding common stock in the open market or in privately negotiated transactions from time to time. Any repurchases by us will comply with the requirements of Rule&#160;10b&#8209;18 under the Exchange Act and any applicable requirements of the 1940 Act. Unless extended by our Board, the repurchase program will terminate on the earlier of June&#160;30, 2027&#160;or the repurchase of $10.0 million of our common stock. During the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, we did not make any repurchases of our common stock under our stock repurchase program. From the date of the inception of our&#160;stock repurchase program through March 31, 2026, we repurchased 167,465 shares of our common stock at an average price of $11.22 on the open market at a total cost of $1.9 million. From time to time, our&#160;Board assesses the size and effectiveness of the stock repurchase program and could elect to increase or decrease the size of the program in the future.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">At March 31, 2026, the&#160;outstanding principal balance under the Key Facility was $45.0&#160;million. At&#160;December 31, 2025, there was no outstanding principal balance under the Key Facility.&#160;As of March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, we had borrowing capacity under the Key Facility of $105.0&#160;million and $150.0, respectively.&#160;At March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, $23.3&#160;million and $49.6&#160;million, respectively, was available for borrowing under the Key Facility, subject to existing terms and advance rates.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">At March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, the outstanding principal balance under the&#160;NYL Facility was $181.0&#160;million. As of March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, we had borrowing capacity under the NYL Facility of $69.0&#160;million. At March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, $2.6&#160;million and $1.9&#160;million, respectively, was available for borrowing under the NYL Facility, subject to existing terms and advance rates.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">At March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;December 31, 2025, the outstanding principal balance under the Nuveen Facility was&#160;$90.0 million. As of March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;December 31, 2025, we had borrowing capacity under the Nuveen Facility of&#160;$110.0 million. At March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;December 31, 2025,&#160;$22.3 million and $12.1&#160;million, respectively, was available for borrowing under the Nuveen Facility, subject to existing terms and advance rates.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On October 17, 2024, the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (the &#8220;2031 Note Purchase Agreement&#8221;), by and among the Company, and each purchaser named therein, in connection with the issuance and sale of $20.0 million aggregate principal of the Company&#8217;s 7.125% convertible notes due 2031 (the &#8220;2031 Convertible Notes&#8221;). At March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;December 31, 2025, the aggregate outstanding principal balance of the 2031 Convertible Notes was $2.8 million.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On September 4, 2025, the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (the &#8220;2030&#160;Note Purchase Agreement&#8221;), by and among the Company, and each purchaser named therein, in connection with the issuance and sale of $40.0 million aggregate principal of the Company&#8217;s 5.50% convertible notes due 2030&#160;(the &#8220;2030&#160;Convertible Notes&#8221;). At March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;December 31, 2025, the aggregate outstanding principal balance of the 2030&#160;Convertible Notes was $16.5&#160;million and&#160;$31.5 million, respectively.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Our operating activities used&#160;cash of $42.1&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2026, and our financing activities used&#160;cash of $27.3&#160;million for the same period. Our operating activities used cash primarily to purchase investments in portfolio companies offset by cash provided by principal payments received on our debt investme<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">nts. Our financing activities </span>used<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> cash primarily to repay our 2026&#160;Notes</span>&#160;and to pay distributions to our stockholders partially<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;offset by advances on our Key Facility.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Our operating activities used cash of&#160;$13.2&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2025, and our financing activities used&#160;cash of&#160;$10.2 million for the same period. Our operating activities used cash primarily to purchase investments in portfolio companies partially offset by cash provided by principal payments received on our debt investments. Our financing activities used cash primarily to repay our 2022 Asset-Backed Notes and to pay distributions to our stockholders partially offset by an advance on our Nuveen Facility and the sale of shares through our ATM for net proceeds of&#160;$3.6&#160;million.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">Our primary use of available funds is to make debt investments in portfolio companies and for general corporate purposes. We expect to raise additional equity and debt capital opportunistically as needed and, subject to market conditions, to support our future growth to the extent permitted by the 1940 Act.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In order to remain subject to taxation as a RIC, we intend to distribute to our stockholders all or substantially all of our investment company taxable income. In addition, as a BDC, we are required to maintain asset coverage of at least 150%. This requirement limits the amount that we may borrow.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">We believe that our current cash, cash generated from operations, and funds available from our Credit Facilities will be sufficient to meet our working capital and capital expenditure commitments for at least the next 12&#160;months.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i><b>Credit Facilities</b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Key Facility</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">We entered into the Key Facility effective November&#160;4, 2013. On February 26, 2026, we amended the Key Facility, among other things, (i) to make Michael P. Balkin and&#160;Paul G. Seitz each an&#160;&#8220;Authorized Person&#8221;, (ii) to amend certain requirements to make a debt investment eligible for the borrowing base and (ii)&#160;to amend certain concentration limits. On June 20, 2024, we amended the Key Facility, among other things, (i) to extend the date on which we may request advances under the Key Facility to June 20, 2027 and to extend the maturity date to June 20, 2029 and (ii) to amend the interest rate to be based on the rate of interest published in The Wall Street Journal as the prime rate in the United States plus 0.10%, with an interest&#160;rate floor of 4.10%. Prior to June 20, 2024, the interest rate on the Key Facility was based on Prime plus 0.25%, with a prime rate floor of&#160;4.25%. The prime rate was&#160;6.75%&#160;as of March 31, 2026&#160;and December 31, 2025. The interest rate&#160;in effect was&#160;6.85%&#160;as of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025. The Key Facility requires the payment of an unused line fee in an amount up to 0.75% of any unborrowed amount available under the facility annually.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">On June 29, 2023, we amended the Key Facility to, among other things, increase the commitment amount to $150 million and to increase the amount of the accordion feature which now allows the potential increase in the total commitment amount to $300 million. The Key Facility is collateralized by debt investments held by Credit II and permits an advance rate of up to sixty&#160;percent (60%) of eligible debt investments held by Credit II. The Key Facility contains covenants that, among other things, require us to maintain a minimum net worth, to restrict the debt investments securing the Key Facility to certain criteria for qualified debt investments and to comply with portfolio company concentration limits as defined in the related loan agreement. After the period during which we may request advances under the Key Facility (or the &#8220;Revolving Period&#8221;), we may not request new advances, and we must repay the outstanding advances under the Key Facility as of such date, at such times and in such amounts as are necessary to maintain compliance with the terms and conditions of the Key Facility, particularly the condition that the principal balance of the Key Facility not exceed sixty&#160;percent (60%) of the aggregate principal balance of our eligible debt investments to our portfolio companies.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>NYL Facility</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">HFI is a wholly-owned subsidiary of HSLFI. HFI entered into the NYL Facility with the NYL Noteholders for an aggregate purchase price of up to $100.0 million, with an accordion feature of up to $200.0 million at the mutual discretion and agreement of HSLFI and the NYL Noteholders. On June 1, 2018, HSLFI sold or contributed to HFI certain secured loans made to certain portfolio companies pursuant to the Sale and Servicing Agreement. Any notes issued by HFI are collateralized by all investments held by HFI and permit an advance rate of up to 67% of the aggregate principal amount of eligible debt investments. All advances under the NYL Facility are&#160;scheduled to mature in June 2030.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">On May 24, 2023, we amended the&#160;NYL Facility to, among other things,&#160;increase&#160;the commitment by $50.0 million to enable our&#160;wholly-owned subsidiary to issue up to $250.0 million of secured notes. On April 25, 2025, we amended the&#160;NYL Facility to, among other things, extend the investment period to June 5, 2027. In addition, the amendment amended the interest rate for advances made after April 25, 2025, fixing the interest rate at the greater of (i) 4.60% and (ii) the Three Year I Curve plus 2.95% with the interest rate to be reset on any advance date.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Under the terms of the NYL Facility, we are required to maintain a reserve cash balance, which may be used to pay monthly interest and principal payments on the NYL Facility. We have&#160;segregated these funds and classified them as restricted investments in money market funds. At March 31, 2026&#160;and December 31, 2025, there were approximately&#160;$1.4 million of such restricted investments.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">There were $181.0&#160;million in notes issued to the NYL Noteholders as of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025 at an interest rate of 6.57%. As of March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, we had borrowing capacity under the NYL Facility of $69.0&#160;million. At March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, $2.6&#160;million and $1.9&#160;million, respectively, was available for borrowing, subject to existing terms and advance rates.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><i>Nuveen Facility</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">HFII entered into the Nuveen Facility with the Nuveen Noteholders for an aggregate purchase price of up to $100.0 million, with an accordion feature of up to $200.0 million at the mutual discretion and agreement us and the Nuveen Noteholders. On June 21, 2024, we sold or contributed to HFII certain secured loans made to certain portfolio companies pursuant to the Sale and Servicing Agreement. Any notes issued by HFII are collateralized by all investments held by HFII and permit an advance rate of up to 67.5% of the aggregate principal amount of eligible debt investments. The Nuveen Facility bore interest, payable monthly, determined at a rate per annum equal to the greater of (i) the yield for the United States Treasury constant maturity 3-year and 5-year in the most recent statistical release published by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System designated as &#8220;Selected Interest Rates (Daily) &#8211; H.15&#8221; interpolated to a 4.88-year weighted average life (the &#8220;Pricing Benchmark&#8221;) plus 3.15% and (ii) 5.00%.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">On May 23, 2025, we amended the&#160;Nuveen&#160;Facility to, among other things, extend the investment period to June 21, 2028 and the maturity date to June 10, 2034, and increase&#160;the commitment by $100.0 million which&#160;enables our&#160;wholly-owned subsidiary to issue up to $200.0 million of secured notes.&#160;In addition, the amendment amended the interest rate for advances made after May 23, 2025, fixing the interest rate at the greater of (i) 5.00% and (ii) the Pricing Benchmark plus 2.95%.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">Under the terms of the Nuveen Facility, we are required to maintain a reserve cash balance, which may be used to pay monthly interest and principal payments on the Nuveen Facility. We have&#160;segregated these funds and classified them as restricted investments in money market funds. At March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;December 31, 2025, there were approximately&#160;$1.3 million and&#160;$1.1&#160;million, respectively, of such restricted investments.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">There were&#160;$90.0 million&#160;in notes issued to the Nuveen Noteholders as of March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;December 31, 2025&#160;at an interest rate of&#160;7.21%. As of March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;December 31, 2025, we had borrowing capacity under the Nuveen Facility of&#160;$110.0&#160;million. At March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;December 31, 2025,&#160;$22.3 million and $12.1&#160;million, respectively, was available for borrowing, subject to existing terms and advance rates.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i><b>Unsecured Notes</b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><i>2026 Notes</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">On March 30, 2021, we issued and sold an aggregate principal amount of $57.5 million of 4.875% notes due in 2026. The amount of 2026 Notes issued and sold included the full exercise by the underwriters of their option to purchase $7.5 million in aggregate principal of additional notes. The 2026 Notes had&#160;a stated maturity of March 30, 2026 and could have been redeemed in whole or in part at our option at any time or from time to time on or after March 30, 2023 at a redemption price of $25 per security plus accrued and unpaid interest. The 2026 Notes bore&#160;interest at a rate of 4.875% per year, payable quarterly on March 30, June 30, September 30 and December 30 of each year. The 2026 Notes were our direct unsecured obligations and (i) ranked equally in right of payment with our current and future unsecured indebtedness; (ii) were&#160;senior in right of payment to any of our future indebtedness that expressly provides it is subordinated to the 2026 Notes; (iii) were effectively subordinated to all of our existing and future secured indebtedness (including indebtedness that is initially unsecured to which we subsequently grant&#160;security), to the extent of the value of the assets securing such indebtedness, and (iv) were structurally subordinated to all existing and future indebtedness and other obligations of any of our subsidiaries. The 2026 Notes were listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol &#8220;HTFB&#8221;. On January 28, 2026, we redeemed all of&#160;the outstanding principal balance of the 2026 Notes plus accrued interest.&#160;We accelerated $0.1&#160;million of unamortized debt issuance costs related to the 2026 Notes.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>2027 Notes</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">On June 15, 2022, we issued and sold an aggregate principal amount of $50.0 million of 6.25% notes due in 2027 and on July 11, 2022, pursuant to the underwriters&#8217; 30 day option to purchase additional notes, we sold an additional $7.5 million of such notes (collectively, the &#8220;2027 Notes&#8221;). The 2027 Notes have a stated maturity of June 15, 2027 and may be redeemed in whole or in part at our option at any time or from time to time on or after June 15, 2024 at a redemption price of $25 per security plus accrued and unpaid interest. The 2027 Notes bear interest at a rate of 6.25% per year, payable quarterly on March 30, June 30, September 30 and December 30 of each year, commencing on September 30, 2022. The 2027 Notes are our direct unsecured obligations and (i) rank equally in right of payment with our current and future unsecured indebtedness; (ii) are senior in right of payment to any of our future indebtedness that expressly provides it is subordinated to the 2027 Notes; (iii) are effectively subordinated to all of our existing and future secured indebtedness (including indebtedness that is initially unsecured to which we subsequently grant&#160;security), to the extent of the value of the assets securing such indebtedness, and (iv) are structurally subordinated to all existing and future indebtedness and other obligations of any of our subsidiaries. As of March 31, 2026, we were in material compliance with the terms of the 2027 Notes. The 2027 Notes are listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol &#8220;HTFC&#8221;.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>2028</i>&#160;<i>Notes</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;">On December 15, 2025, we issued and sold an aggregate principal amount of $57.5&#160;million of 7.00% notes due in 2028 in a private transaction. The 2028&#160;Notes have a stated maturity of December 15, 2028&#160;and may be redeemed in whole or in part at any time at our option&#160;through&#160;June 15, 2028,&#160;at a redemption price equal to the greater of: (1)(a) the sum of the present values of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest thereon discounted to the redemption date on a semi-annual basis at the Treasury Rate plus 50 basis points less (b) interest accrued to the date of redemption, and (2) 100% of the principal amount of the 2028 Notes to be redeemed, plus, in either case, accrued and unpaid interest thereon to, but not including, the redemption date. On or after June 15, 2028, we may redeem the 2028 Notes, in whole or in part, at any time and from time to time, at a redemption price equal to 100% of the principal amount of the 2028 Notes being redeemed plus accrued and unpaid interest there onto the date of redemption.&#160;The 2028&#160;Notes bear interest at a rate of 7.00% per year, payable semi-annually on June 15 and December 15&#160;of each year, commencing on June 15, 2026. The 2028&#160;Notes are our direct unsecured obligations and (i) rank equally in right of payment with our current and future unsecured indebtedness; (ii) are senior in right of payment to any of our future indebtedness that expressly provides it is subordinated to the 2028&#160;Notes; (iii) are effectively subordinated to all of our existing and future secured indebtedness (including indebtedness that is initially unsecured to which we subsequently grant&#160;security), to the extent of the value of the assets securing such indebtedness, and (iv) are structurally subordinated to all existing and future indebtedness and other obligations of any of our subsidiaries. As of March 31, 2026, we were in material compliance with the terms of the 2028&#160;Notes.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i><b>Convertible Notes</b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>2030&#160;Convertible&#160;Notes</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">On September 4, 2025, we&#160;entered into the 2030&#160;Note Purchase Agreement, by and among us and&#160;each purchaser named therein, in connection with the issuance and sale of $40.0 million aggregate principal of our 5.50% 2030&#160;Convertible Notes in a&#160;transaction&#160;exempt from registration pursuant to Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. We received net proceeds (before expenses) from the sale of the 2030&#160;Convertible Notes of approximately $36.6 million.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The 2030&#160;Convertible Notes have a stated maturity of&#160;September 4, 2030, unless earlier converted or repurchased in accordance with their terms. The 2030&#160;Convertible&#160;Notes bear interest at a rate of 5.50% per year, payable monthly in arrears on the last day of each calendar month, beginning on September 30, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">At any time on or after October 4, 2025, at our&#160;sole option, we may redeem, from time to time, the 2030&#160;Convertible Notes in whole or in part, out of funds legally available for such redemption, at 100% of the principal amount prepaid plus accrued but unpaid interest to but excluding the date of prepayment.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Each holder of a 2030&#160;Convertible Note has the right, at such holder&#8217;s option, to convert any such 2030&#160;Convertible Note, at any time on or after October 4, 2025 and prior to the close of business on the business day immediately preceding the maturity date, into such number of shares of our common stock&#160;equal to the principal balance of the 2030&#160;Convertible Note being converted on the conversion date plus the accrued but unpaid interest on the 2030&#160;Convertible Note as of the conversion date, divided by the greater of (i) volume-weighted average closing sale price for the five trading days immediately prior to the relevant conversion date, or (ii) our&#160;most recently reported NAV per share immediately prior to the date of exercise.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">No holder of 2030&#160;Convertible Notes may exercise its conversion right if upon conversion the holder would receive shares that would cause funds and accounts managed by the investment adviser to such funds and accounts and any person controlled by the parent company of such investment adviser to beneficially own in the aggregate more than 4.99% of the shares outstanding at such time.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The 2030&#160;Convertible Notes are not listed on any exchange and may not be transferred without our consent.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">During the three months ended March 31, 2026, the holders of a portion of the 2030&#160;Convertible Notes&#160;converted&#160;$15.1&#160;million in outstanding principal of the 2030&#160;Convertible Notes plus accrued but unpaid interest on such outstanding principal as of the conversion date into&#160;2,118,250 shares of common&#160;stock at a weighted average conversion price of&#160;$7.12 together with cash in lieu of fractional shares, in accordance with noteholder conversion notice.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">As of March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;December 31, 2025, the aggregate outstanding principal balance of the 2030&#160;Convertible Notes was&#160;$16.5 million and $31.5&#160;million, respectively.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>2031 Convertible&#160;Notes</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">On October 17, 2024, we&#160;entered into the 2031 Note Purchase Agreement, by and among us and&#160;each purchaser named therein, in connection with the issuance and sale of $20.0 million aggregate principal of our&#160;7.125% 2031 Convertible Notes&#160;in a transaction exempt from registration pursuant to Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. We received net proceeds (before expenses) from the sale of the 2031&#160;Convertible Notes of approximately $18.6 million.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The 2031&#160;Convertible Notes have a stated maturity of&#160;October 17, 2031, unless earlier converted or repurchased in accordance with their terms. The 2031 Convertible&#160;Notes bear interest at a rate of 7.125% per year, subject to additional interest or repurchase obligation upon certain events, payable quarterly in arrears on March 31, June 30, September 30 and December 31 of each year, beginning on December 31, 2024. If an investment grade rating is not maintained with respect to the 2031&#160;Convertible Notes, additional interest of 1.00% per annum will accrue on the 2031 Convertible Notes until such time as the 2031 Convertible Notes have received an investment grade rating of &#8220;BBB-&#8221; (or its equivalent) or better. We will also be required to pay additional interest of 2.00% per annum (x) on any overdue payment of interest and (y) during the continuance of an Event of Default (as defined in the 2031 Note Purchase Agreement). In addition, on the occurrence of a Change in Control Repurchase Event (as defined in the 2031 Note Purchase Agreement) or Delisting Event (as defined in the 2031 Note Purchase Agreement), we will generally be required to make an offer to purchase the outstanding 2031&#160;Convertible Notes at a price equal to 100% of the principal amount of such 2031 Convertible Notes plus accrued and unpaid interest to the repurchase date.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">At any time on or after April 17, 2025, at our&#160;sole option, we may redeem, from time to time, the 2031 Convertible Notes in whole or in part, out of funds legally available for such redemption, at 100% of the principal amount prepaid plus accrued but unpaid interest to but excluding the date of prepayment.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Each holder of a 2031 Convertible Note has the right, at such holder&#8217;s option, to convert any such 2031&#160;Convertible Note, at any time on or after April 17, 2025 and prior to the close of business on the business day immediately preceding the maturity date, into such number of shares of our common stock equal to the principal balance of the 2031&#160;Convertible Note being converted on the conversion date plus the accrued but unpaid interest on the 2031 Convertible Note as of the conversion date, divided by the greater of (i) volume-weighted average closing sale price for the five trading days immediately prior to the relevant conversion date, or (ii) our&#160;most recently reported NAV per share immediately prior to the date of exercise.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">No holder of 2031&#160;Convertible Notes may exercise its conversion right if upon conversion the holder would receive shares that would cause funds and accounts managed by the investment adviser to such funds and accounts and any person controlled by the parent company of such investment adviser to beneficially own in the aggregate more than 4.99% of the shares outstanding at such time.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The 2031&#160;Convertible Notes are not listed on any exchange and may not be transferred without our consent.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">During the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, the holders of&#160;the 2031&#160;Convertible Notes did not convert any of the 2031 Convertible Notes.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">As of March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, the aggregate outstanding principal balance of the 2031&#160;Convertible Notes was&#160;$2.8 million.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Other assets</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">As of March 31, 2026 and&#160;December 31, 2025, other assets were $9.9&#160;million and $9.1&#160;million, respectively, which were&#160;primarily comprised of debt issuance costs and prepaid expenses.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In the normal course of business, we are party to financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk. These consist primarily of unfunded commitments to extend credit, in the form of loans, to our portfolio companies. Unfunded commitments to provide funds to portfolio companies are not reflected on our balance sheet. Our unfunded commitments may be significant from time to time. As of March 31, 2026, we had&#160;unfunded commitments of $155.0&#160;million. This includes&#160;$15.0&#160;million of&#160;undrawn revolver commitments. These commitments are subject to the same underwriting and ongoing portfolio maintenance requirements as are the financial instruments that we hold on our balance sheet. In addition, these commitments are often subject to financial or non-financial milestones and other conditions to borrowing that must be achieved before the commitment can be drawn. Since these commitments may expire without being drawn upon, the total commitment amount does not necessarily represent future cash requirements. We regularly monitor our unfunded commitments and anticipated refinancings, maturities and capital raising, to ensure that we have sufficient liquidity to fund unfunded commitments. As of March 31, 2026, we reasonably believed that our assets would provide adequate financial resources to satisfy all of our unfunded commitments.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In addition to the Credit Facilities, we have certain commitments pursuant to our Investment Management Agreement entered into with our Advisor. We have agreed to pay a fee for investment advisory and management services consisting of two components (1)&#160;a base management fee equal to a&#160;percentage of the value of our gross assets less cash or cash equivalents, and (2)&#160;a two-part incentive fee. We have also entered into a contract with our Advisor to serve as our administrator. Payments under the Administration Agreement are equal to an amount based upon our allocable portion of our Advisor&#8217;s overhead in performing its obligations under the agreement, including rent, fees and other expenses inclusive of our allocable portion of the compensation of our Chief Financial Officer and Chief Compliance Officer and their respective staffs. See Note&#160;3 to our consolidated financial statements for additional information regarding our Investment Management Agreement and our Administration Agreement.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The incentive fee on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income is subject to a fee cap and deferral mechanism which is determined based upon a look-back period of up to three&#160;years and is expensed when incurred. For this purpose, the Incentive Fee Look-back Period includes the relevant calendar quarter and the 11 preceding full calendar quarters. Each quarterly incentive fee payable on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income is subject to the Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism. The Incentive Fee Cap is equal to (a)&#160;20.00% of Cumulative Pre-Incentive Fee Net Return during the Incentive Fee Look-back Period less (b)&#160;cumulative incentive fees of any kind paid to our&#160;Advisor during the Incentive Fee Look-back Period. To the extent the Incentive Fee Cap is zero or a negative value in any calendar quarter, we will not pay an incentive fee on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income to our&#160;Advisor in that quarter. To the extent that the payment of incentive fees on Pre-Incentive Fee Net Investment Income is limited by the Incentive Fee Cap, the payment of such fees will be deferred and paid in subsequent calendar quarters up to three&#160;years after their date of deferment, subject to certain limitations, which are set forth in the Investment Management Agreement. During the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025,&#160;the Incentive Fee Cap and Deferral Mechanism resulted in deferral of&#160;$0.4&#160;million and&#160;$2.1&#160;million, respectively, of incentive fee which may become subject to payment up to three&#160;years after the date of deferment. As of March 31, 2026&#160;and December 31, 2025, the total amount subject to recoupment was&#160;$28.2 million and $28.0&#160;million, respectively. Commencing with the quarter ending March 31, 2025 and terminated with the quarter ending&#160;December 31, 2025, our Advisor agreed to waive the portion of its quarterly income incentive fee, if any, if and to the extent that, after payment of such portion, our&#160;net investment income per share for such quarter would be less than the quarterly distribution per share declared in such quarter. During the three months ended March 31, 2025, our&#160;Advisor did not earn an income incentive fee.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 11pt;"><b><i>Distributions</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In order to qualify and be subject to tax as a RIC, we must meet certain source-of-income, asset diversification and annual distribution requirements. Generally, in order to qualify as a RIC, we must derive at least 90% of our gross income for each tax&#160;year from dividends, interest, payments with respect to certain securities, loans, gains from the sale or other disposition of stock, securities or foreign currencies, income derived from certain publicly traded partnerships, or other income (including but not limited to gains from options, futures or forward contracts)&#160;derived with respect to our business of investing in stock, securities or other currencies. We must also meet certain asset diversification requirements at the end of each quarter of each tax&#160;year. Failure to meet these diversification requirements on the last day of a quarter may result in us having to dispose of certain investments quickly in order to prevent the loss of RIC status. Any such dispositions could be made at disadvantageous prices or times, and may cause us to incur substantial losses.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In addition, in order to be subject to tax as a RIC and to avoid the imposition of corporate-level tax on the income and gains we distribute to our stockholders in respect of any tax&#160;year, we are required under the Code to distribute as dividends to our stockholders out of assets legally available for distribution each tax&#160;year an amount generally at least equal to 90% of the sum of our net ordinary income and net short-term capital gains in excess of net long-term capital losses, if any. Additionally, in order to avoid the imposition of a U.S. federal excise tax, we are required to distribute, in respect of each calendar&#160;year, dividends to our stockholders of an amount at least equal to the sum of 98% of our calendar&#160;year net ordinary income (taking into account certain deferrals and elections); 98.2% of our capital gain net income (adjusted for certain ordinary losses) for the one&#160;year period ending on October&#160;31 of such calendar&#160;year; and any net ordinary income and capital gain net income for preceding calendar&#160;years that were not distributed during such calendar&#160;years and on which we previously did not incur any U.S. federal corporate-level income tax. If we fail to qualify as a RIC for any reason and become subject to corporate-level income&#160;tax, the resulting corporate-level income taxes could substantially reduce our net assets, the amount of income available for distribution and the amount of our distributions. Such a failure would have a material adverse effect on us and our stockholders. In addition, we could be required to recognize unrealized gains, incur substantial taxes and interest and make substantial distributions in order to re-qualify as a RIC. We cannot assure stockholders that they will receive any distributions.</p>
